CVE-2021-4178 describes arbitrary code execution in Fabric8 Kubernetes Client due to unsafe YAML parsing: a local privileged attacker can supply malicious YAML that is parsed with SnakeYAML default construction. The failed new-unified row uses exact vulnerable checkout 1d1b3d404836871c4d0fc0a35dafe5d40369b519. In that checkout, Serialization.unmarshal wraps the supplied InputStream, peeks at the first non-whitespace byte, and sends non-JSON input into unmarshalYaml. unmarshalYaml constructs SnakeYAML with new Yaml(), calls yaml.load(is), serializes the resulting object map to JSON, and then maps it into the requested Kubernetes resource type. The default SnakeYAML constructor is the vulnerable deserialization/code-generation boundary. Fix commit 445103004d1ed3153d5abb272473451d05891e39 imports SafeConstructor and changes the parser construction to new Yaml(new SafeConstructor()), binding the advisory to source-backed YAML input routing, unsafe SnakeYAML construction, and YAML load of attacker-controlled content.

CVE-2022-44262 / GHSA-65hj-9ppw-77xc describes remote code execution in ff4j versions >= 1.8.1 and < 1.9, patched in 1.9. The exact source snapshot 7c34409d320ed1c917c4ec4ac72a99661c4e446f is the 1.8.13 tag and is inside the affected range. The GHSA-referenced fix commit 62d03140f3bfbd380d0f4b4e5a94dcb8baa9d9c6 merges PR #625 and is contained in tag 1.9. The 1.9 fix adds Property.class.isAssignableFrom and FlippingStrategy.class.isAssignableFrom checks in PropertyFactory, XmlParser, PropertiesParser, and YamlParser. The reviewed spans below bind the exact 1.8.13 source snapshot to the public arbitrary-class-instantiation RCE path without relying on eval hits, generated source-sink annotations, or non-final sidecar proxies.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2022-4963 describes SQL injection in FOLIO Spring Module Core schema-name handling up to 1.1.5, involving HibernateSchemaService.schemaExists and schema names derived from tenant input. The failed new-unified row uses exact vulnerable checkout e93b5ddd3022b81abf8ae81da8d3a740186f456e. In that checkout, SchemaService.getSchema builds a schema name from the tenant and artifact and only replaces hyphens with underscores, with no allowlist validation. HibernateSchemaService.getSettings stores that schema as HIBERNATE_DEFAULT_SCHEMA, and public createTenant, deleteTenant, and schemaExists flows call schemaExists using tenant-derived schema values. The private schemaExists(Connection, String) builds an information_schema query template containing schema_name = '%s' and executes Statement.executeQuery(String.format(queryTemplate, schema)), directly interpolating the schema value into SQL. Fix commit d374a5f77e6b58e36f0e0e4419be18b95edcd7ff changes schemaExists to a PreparedStatement with a ? parameter and statement.setString(1, schema), and adds a SchemaService regex allowlist [a-zA-Z0-9_]+. This binds the advisory to source-backed tenant-to-schema derivation, unsanitized SQL string formatting, and the database query sink.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2025-24961 / GHSA-2ccp-vqmv-4r4x describes S3Proxy filesystem and filesystem-nio2 storage backends allowing authenticated clients to traverse outside the intended backing directory. In the reviewed exact prepatch checkout 83b159ee4b9ffcf3f7d91313592fad88feb3b621, AbstractNio2BlobStore uses the request container as a root component and directly resolves attacker-controlled list prefix or object key into filesystem Paths: list() builds pathPrefix as root.resolve(container).resolve(prefix), getBlob() builds root.resolve(container).resolve(key), putBlob() builds root.resolve(container).resolve(blob.getMetadata().getName()) and a similarly derived temp path, removeBlob() deletes containerPath.resolve(key), and getBlobAccess()/setBlobAccess() read or change permissions on root.resolve(container).resolve(key). These paths are used for Files read/write/delete/permission operations without a containment check ensuring the normalized result still starts with the container directory. The S3Proxy 2.6.0 fix commit 86b6ee4749aa163a78e7898efc063617ed171980 is a single-parent commit whose parent is this exact checkout and is titled Prevent parent path traversal in filesystem-nio2; it adds checkValidPath(containerPath, path) and invokes it on list, get, put, delete, get access, and set access paths before filesystem operations. The broader advisory also mentions apache/jclouds@b0819e0 for the non-nio2 backend; this reviewed-source row only admits the source-backed S3Proxy filesystem-nio2 path fixed in this repository commit.

CVE-2025-27505 describes a GeoServer missing-authorization issue where the default REST API security filter protects /rest and subpaths but not extension-style REST index paths such as /rest.html, allowing the REST API index to disclose installed extensions. The exact vulnerable source snapshot dab1947ce0d1a46418ae690734be5ccc5252057b is the GeoServer 2.26.2 release tag, immediately before the fixed 2.26.3 release commit 4a7a6881894a879f097ca2f04d62733fcdaa2937. In the vulnerable default data directory security/config.xml, the rest ServiceLoginFilterChain path is only /rest/** and the gwc ServiceLoginFilterChain path is only /gwc/rest/**. These Ant-style subpath patterns do not cover extension suffix requests such as /rest.html or /gwc/rest.html. The fixed 2.26.3 compare updates data/release/security/config.xml and sample security configs so rest uses /rest.*,/rest/** and gwc uses /gwc/rest.*,/gwc/rest/**, matching the public workaround text. This binds the public advisory, exact vulnerable release, and source-backed default security filter path gap without relying on generated findings or non-final sidecar hits.

The exact vulnerable source snapshot dab1947ce0d1a46418ae690734be5ccc5252057b is the GeoServer 2.26.2 release tag, immediately before the fixed 2.26.3 release commit 4a7a6881894a879f097ca2f04d62733fcdaa2937. In the vulnerable default data directory security/config.xml, the rest ServiceLoginFilterChain path is only /rest/** and the gwc ServiceLoginFilterChain path is only /gwc/rest/**. These Ant-style subpath patterns do not cover extension suffix requests such as /rest.html or /gwc/rest.html. The fixed 2.26.3 compare updates data/release/security/config.xml and sample security configs so rest uses /rest.*,/rest/** and gwc uses /gwc/rest.*,/gwc/rest/**, matching the public workaround text. This binds the public advisory, exact vulnerable release, and source-backed default security filter path gap without relying on generated findings or non-final sidecar hits.

CVE-2025-30145 / GHSA-gr67-pwcv-76gf describes GeoServer denial of service from malicious Jiffle scripts reachable either as WMS dynamic styling rendering transformations or as WPS processes. The exact vulnerable GeoServer snapshot dab1947ce0d1a46418ae690734be5ccc5252057b is the 2.26.2 release tag, and the fixed GeoServer snapshot 4a7a6881894a879f097ca2f04d62733fcdaa2937 is the 2.26.3 release tag listed as fixed. In the vulnerable checkout, src/pom.xml uses gt.version 32.2 and jaiext.version 1.1.27, while WMS and WPS depend on gt-process-raster, the raster process family that exposes ras:Jiffle in GeoServer rendering transformations and WPS process execution. GeoServer WMS production code extracts SLD FeatureTypeStyle transformations and DirectRasterRenderer applies them through RenderingTransformationHelper; GeoServer test SLDs show ras:Jiffle with a script literal in the same transformation shape. GeoServer WPS production code dispatches ExecuteType to Execute.run and DefaultProcessManager creates and executes the requested GeoTools process with request inputs. The 2.26.3 line updates the GeoTools/JAI-EXT dependency set, including jaiext.version 1.1.31; GeoServer PR #8418 is the 2.26.x backport titled GEOS-11770 Update to jai-ext 1.1.31. In JAI-EXT 1.1.31, the Jiffle compiler/runtime adds MAX_ITERATIONS_KEY, DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS 200, checkLoopIterations(), and inserts checkLoopIterations() into generated while and until loop bodies, with documentation stating that Jiffle limits maximum loop iterations per pixel and throws an exception. This binds the GeoServer entry points and dependency boundary in the vulnerable checkout to the fixed-version Jiffle loop guard without relying on generated findings or non-final sidecar rows.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2023-41044 describes partial path traversal in Graylog Support Bundle download/delete APIs: an authenticated admin can access or delete files in sibling directories whose names start with the support-bundle directory prefix. The failed new-unified row uses exact vulnerable checkout d970230b6f3ecb83e07dd43df56428d1421c40e9. In that checkout, SupportBundleResource exposes GET /system/debug/support/bundle/download/{filename} and DELETE /system/debug/support/bundle/{filename}, passing the path parameter filename to SupportBundleService.downloadBundle and deleteBundle. Both service methods call ensureFileWithinBundleDir(filename), then resolve filename under bundleDir and copy or delete the resulting path. The vulnerable ensureFileWithinBundleDir compares bundleDir.resolve(filename).toFile().getCanonicalPath().startsWith(bundleDir.toFile().getCanonicalPath()), which is a string prefix check rather than a path-component containment check, so sibling paths such as support-bundle-test can satisfy the prefix. Fix commit 02b8792e6f4b829f0c1d87fcbf2d58b73458b938 changes the helper to compare normalized absolute Path values and updates both download and delete call sites. This binds the advisory to source-backed filename path parameter intake, weak canonical string-prefix validation, and file read/delete sinks.

CVE-2023-24057 describes Zip Slip style path traversal in HL7 FHIR Core Libraries before 5.6.92, where crafted ZIP or TGZ archives for terminology cache, NPM packages, or comparison archives can carry unsafe entry names. The failed new-unified row uses exact vulnerable checkout 7b22d0355b1b12448e50b9cbfe2a8ae63f2ee828. In that checkout, the R4B and R5 TerminologyCacheManager initialize terminology cache data by downloading tx-cache ZIP content, passing it to unzip, building output paths with Utilities.path(targetDir, ze.getName()), checking the unnormalized string with startsWith(targetDir), and then creating directories or writing entry bytes with TextFile.streamToFileNoClose. Scanner.genScanOutput downloads comparison.zip and Scanner.unzip concatenates destDirectory plus entry.getName directly, then writes files with extractFile or creates directories, without normalizing and verifying destination containment. NpmPackage.readStream also consumes TGZ entry names and loads files without rejecting traversal segments before the fix. Fix commit b50aec59124416b7315a49220cfc3999223414cc adds normalized path checks to terminology cache and scanner ZIP extraction and rejects TGZ entry names containing dot-dot. This binds the advisory to source-backed archive entry name intake, incomplete path traversal validation, and filesystem extraction sinks for ZIP-based cache/comparison archives.

CVE-2023-28465 describes an incomplete fix for CVE-2023-24057 in HL7 FHIR Core Libraries package decompression: normalized archive output paths were still checked with a character string prefix rather than path-component containment, allowing traversal into sibling directories whose names start with the allowed directory name. The failed new-unified row uses exact vulnerable checkout 0b8e2c39841b51def04e29d3b745602517602d5b. In that checkout, both R5 and R4B TerminologyCacheManager.initialize download tx-cache ZIP content and call unzip with cacheFolder as targetDir. The unzip methods compute String path = Path.of(Utilities.path(targetDir, ze.getName())).normalize().toFile().getAbsolutePath(), then check if !path.startsWith(targetDir). Because this is String.startsWith, a normalized absolute path under a sibling directory such as cache2 can still start with the targetDir string cache. The methods then create directories or write entry bytes to path. Fix commit 909f7e64fea6532a00b3eb8904bf620fc3cae6d1 changes path to a Path, stores pathString separately for filesystem writes, and checks path.startsWith(Path.of(targetDir).normalize()), using path semantics instead of character-prefix semantics. This binds the advisory to source-backed terminology cache ZIP entry intake, incomplete normalized path containment validation, and filesystem extraction sinks.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2025-26511 describes an RBAC bypass in Instaclustr Cassandra-Lucene-Index where authenticated Cassandra users can execute Lucene-index SELECT queries without the normal Cassandra statement authorization path. The failed new-unified row uses exact vulnerable checkout 75b83c55705e38a4e93fbeb3d841779810074924, corresponding to the affected cassandra-4.0.16-1.0.0 source snapshot. In that checkout, the plugin installs a custom IndexQueryHandler as Cassandra CQL query handler. IndexQueryHandler.processStatement prepares bind variables and increments metrics, then intercepts SelectStatement instances carrying Lucene expressions and returns executeLuceneQuery before calling the fallback execute(statement, state, options, requestTime). Unlike Cassandra regular statement execution, this intercepted branch does not call statement.authorize(state.getClientState) or statement.validate(state.getClientState) before evaluating the SELECT and reading data. executeLuceneQuery validates only the Lucene expression, constructs read commands, and either delegates to execute(statement, ...) or performs sorted Lucene reads through executeSortedLuceneQuery and LuceneStorageProxy.read, allowing the Lucene query path to bypass RBAC checks for the selected table. Fix commit 44ab4b639c9354a6335f40b1cf6178c745c6e101, released as cassandra-4.0.17-1.0.0, adds statement.authorize(state.getClientState) and statement.validate(state.getClientState) at the start of processStatement before the Lucene interception. This binds the advisory to source-backed CQL SELECT intake, missing statement authorization and validation, and Lucene read execution sinks.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2022-45206 describes SQL injection in JeecgBoot v3.4.3 through the /sys/duplicate/check component. The failed new-unified row uses exact vulnerable checkout d34614c4224ec1af69d0d81329d84fe98e11f694, which is before the source fix f18ced524c9ec13e876bfb74785a1b112cc8b6bb. In that checkout, DuplicateCheckController exposes GET /sys/duplicate/check and binds request parameters into DuplicateCheckVo fields tableName, fieldName, fieldVal, and dataId. The controller checks only tableName and fieldName with SqlInjectionUtil.filterContent and DictQueryBlackListHandler, then calls SysDictMapper.duplicateCheckCountSql or duplicateCheckCountSqlNoDataId. The mapper XML builds SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ${tableName} WHERE ${fieldName} = #{fieldVal}, using MyBatis ${} substitution for tableName and fieldName, so bypassing the identifier filter reaches raw SQL text. In the vulnerable SqlInjectionUtil, SQL comments matching /\*.*\*/ are stripped before keyword checks, and extractvalue/updatexml are not in the default keyword list. The official fix commit is titled sql注入检查更加严格，修复/sys/duplicate/check存在sql注入漏洞 #4129; it adds SQL_ANNOTATION, calls checkSqlAnnotation before lowercasing, stops stripping comments as a bypass, and adds extractvalue/updatexml to keyword filters. This binds the advisory to source-backed request parameter intake, incomplete SQL injection filtering, and MyBatis dynamic SQL table/field substitution sinks.

CVE-2022-20617 / GHSA-jpxj-vgq5-prjc describes Jenkins Docker Commons Plugin 1.17 and earlier failing to sanitize Docker image names or tags, creating an OS command execution vulnerability for users with Item/Configure permission or control over a configured job SCM repository. The reviewed exact source snapshot 2f0fda49452a7653c33de24220c908786f1aa405 is the vulnerable docker-commons-1.17 source snapshot used by the failed row. In that snapshot, DockerRegistryEndpoint.imageName accepts userAndRepo, checks only for null, and either returns userAndRepo unchanged when url is null or prepends the registry host before returning the same unvalidated image/tag string. This image name is part of the Docker command surface used by downstream Jenkins Docker integrations. The fixed commit c069b79c31c5aa80a01b0c462f0dc6b41751f059 adds ImageNameValidator, calls validateUserAndRepo(userAndRepo) from imageName before returning or prefixing the image string, and validates repository name components and tags with explicit patterns; the added tests reject newline command injection examples such as name:tag\necho hello and name\necho hello:tag plus variable-like image/tag inputs. This binds the public advisory, exact vulnerable checkout, source-backed unvalidated Docker image/tag propagation, and the fixed validation boundary.

CVE-2019-10392 / SECURITY-1534 affects Jenkins Git Client Plugin 2.8.4 and earlier because repository URL values supplied to CLI git remote operations were not sufficiently restricted before being passed as operands to git ls-remote, allowing crafted values such as command options, --upload-pack, backquoted commands, or whitespace-separated argument sequences to influence command execution on the Jenkins master. The reviewed 2.8.4 source snapshot exposes getHeadRev, getRemoteReferences, and getRemoteSymbolicReferences as remote-reference lookup APIs equivalent to git ls-remote, delegates those APIs through RemoteGitImpl, and in CliGitAPIImpl builds ArgumentListBuilder("ls-remote") before directly appending the caller-controlled url with args.add(url) and invoking launchCommandWithCredentials. The 2.8.5 SECURITY-1534 fix adds GitClientSecurityTest coverage for malicious URL prefixes, introduces addCheckedRemoteUrl to reject dangerous remote URL strings and insert an end-of-options marker, and replaces these direct args.add(url) calls in the ls-remote paths with addCheckedRemoteUrl(args, url). These source spans provide the reviewed command-injection trace and recall anchors for the vulnerable ls-remote URL handling.

CVE-2025-31720 describes a missing permission check in Jenkins 2.503 and earlier, LTS 2.492.2 and earlier: attackers with Computer/Create permission but without Computer/Extended Read permission can copy an agent and gain access to its configuration. The failed new-unified row uses exact vulnerable checkout dddb4598df25527220a1e0f46d1a0d25217dd4c8. In that checkout, ComputerSet.doCreateItem handles the first POST step for creating a new agent. It checks app.checkPermission(Computer.CREATE), then when mode equals copy, reads the source node name from the from request parameter, resolves Node src = app.getNode(from), serializes the source node with Jenkins.XSTREAM.toXML(src), deserializes it into a new Node, and adds the copied node. There is no src.checkPermission(Computer.EXTENDED_READ) before serializing the source agent configuration. Computer.EXTENDED_READ is a Computer-scoped permission distinct from Computer.CREATE, which is Jenkins-scoped. Fix commit bf32018bf075c06e5df649583557c82d42d8bb5c adds src.checkPermission(Computer.EXTENDED_READ) after resolving the source node and before the XStream copy. This binds the advisory to source-backed HTTP copy-agent intake, missing source-agent extended-read authorization, and source node configuration serialization/copy sinks.

CVE-2025-31721 describes an incomplete agent-copy permission fix in Jenkins 2.503 and earlier, LTS 2.492.2 and earlier: attackers with Computer/Create permission but without Computer/Configure permission can copy an agent containing encrypted secrets in its configuration. The failed new-unified row uses exact vulnerable checkout bf32018bf075c06e5df649583557c82d42d8bb5c, which already contains the CVE-2025-31720 Extended Read check but remains vulnerable for secret-bearing agent configurations. In that checkout, ComputerSet.doCreateItem handles POST agent creation, checks Computer.CREATE, enters mode=copy, resolves the source Node from the from request parameter, checks src.checkPermission(Computer.EXTENDED_READ), then serializes the source node with Jenkins.XSTREAM.toXML(src), immediately deserializes it into a new Node, and adds the copied node. The code does not require Computer.CONFIGURE and does not test whether ExtendedReadRedaction would remove secrets from the source configuration before copying. Fix commit b3651b475302e8dba20fc63c1ff89d144ec652f0 adds a guard after XStream serialization: if the user lacks Computer.CONFIGURE, it applies ExtendedReadRedaction.applyAll(xml), compares the redacted XML to the original, and throws AccessDeniedException when the configuration contains redacted secrets. This binds the advisory to source-backed copy-agent HTTP intake, missing configure-or-secret-redaction authorization, and XStream configuration copy sinks.

CVE-2025-24399 affects Jenkins OpenId Connect Authentication Plugin 4.452.v2849b_d3945fa_ and earlier because usernames obtained from a case-sensitive OpenID Connect provider are handed directly to Jenkins authentication and user lookup without a plugin-level case-sensitivity control. In the vulnerable checkout, doFinishLogin reads the configured username claim from the validated OIDC profile and passes it to loginAndSetUserData. loginAndSetUserData then constructs a UsernamePasswordAuthenticationToken from that exact string, installs it in the security context, and calls User.get2(token), allowing Jenkins user identity resolution to treat differently cased provider usernames as the same Jenkins user under case-insensitive behavior. Version 4.453.v4d7765c854f4 is documented by GHSA/NVD/Jenkins advisory as introducing an advanced username case-sensitivity option defaulting to case-sensitive.

CVE-2020-2261 / GHSA-jq84-6fmm-6qv6 describes OS command execution in Jenkins Perfecto Plugin 1.17 and earlier. Users with Job/Configure permission can configure Perfecto Connect build-wrapper fields so that the plugin executes commands on the Jenkins controller. The reviewed exact source snapshot adabcd9da98628e063bb91198e30ff39a34dc921 corresponds to the vulnerable 1.17 source snapshot used by the failed row. In that snapshot, the DataBoundConstructor stores user-controlled configuration fields including perfectoConnectLocation, perfectoConnectFile, and pcParameters. During setUp, the wrapper reads the Perfecto API key from Jenkins credentials, calls getTunnelId(perfectoConnectLocation, credentials.getCloudName(), apiKey, listener), and getTunnelId builds baseCommand by string-concatenating pcLocation, cloudName, and apiKey, appends pcParameters, then executes the resulting command through cmd.exe /c on Windows or bash -c plus Runtime.getRuntime().exec on Unix. Public advisory text states that Perfecto Plugin 1.18 changes execution to run the specified commands on the agent the build is running on rather than on the controller. The fixed commit 52c09ad2e26416211e4009b095c4f16508b27b8a raw source imports hudson.tasks.CommandInterpreter, builds script = baseCommand + pcParameters, and executes it through getCommandInterpreter(launcher, script), returning Shell(script) on Unix or BatchFile(script) otherwise and calling runner.perform(build, launcher, listener). This binds the advisory, exact vulnerable checkout, source-backed configured-parameter-to-controller-shell-execution path, and fixed-source boundary change.

CVE-2023-24422 / GHSA-76qj-9gwh-pvv3 / Jenkins SECURITY-3016 describe Jenkins Script Security Plugin 1228.vd93135a_2fb_25 and earlier allowing sandboxed Groovy scripts to bypass sandbox protection through map constructor handling, enabling code execution in the Jenkins controller JVM for users allowed to define or run sandboxed scripts. The reviewed exact source snapshot d93135a2fb250c04cc361b0bb1efd809bc63ad08 is tagged 1228.vd93135a_2fb_25, the vulnerable version named by the advisory. In that snapshot, GroovyCallSiteSelector.constructor treats a single Map argument as Groovy's implicit map constructor and returns a zero-argument constructor when no real constructor matches. SandboxInterceptor.onNewInstance then checks only the selected constructor against the whitelist and directly delegates to super.onNewInstance with the original Map argument, so Groovy performs implicit property assignments without the sandbox-aware property-set checks later added by the fix. CVE-2025-31723 / GHSA-hcfh-qjcp-34q9 describes Jenkins Simple Queue Plugin 1.4.6 and earlier not requiring POST requests for multiple HTTP endpoints, allowing CSRF attacks to change and reset the build queue order. The reviewed exact source snapshot c5bc23d6ddd16b0a9792dd05e843a14033e975f1 is the vulnerable source snapshot used by the failed row. In that snapshot, SimpleQueueWidget/index.jelly and SimpleQueueUpdateAction/ajaxBuildQueue.jelly render queue-move controls as plain anchor href links to /simpleMove/move with moveType, itemId, and viewName query parameters. CVE-2025-31722 affects Jenkins Templating Engine Plugin 2.5.3 and earlier because libraries defined in folders are not subject to sandbox protection. In exact vulnerable checkout 0af836f6465f80a078a02c6f2ed2e93dd5056213, TemplateFlowDefinition creates a CpsFlowExecution and invokes TemplatePrimitiveInjector.orchestrate. LibraryStepInjector.injectPrimitives loads configured libraries from the governance hierarchy, iterates their steps, and calls StepWrapperFactory.createFromFilePath(stepFile, libName, libConfig) without passing any sandbox/trust decision. StepWrapperFactory.createFromFilePath builds a library StepWrapper and prepareScript always uses exec.getTrustedShell() to parse the library step source. This causes folder-scoped library steps to run through the trusted shell rather than the sandbox shell. Version 2.5.4 changes LibraryStepInjector to distinguish global providers from non-global providers, sets isSandboxed for non-global/folder libraries, passes that flag into createFromFilePath, and changes prepareScript to use exec.getShell() when step.isSandboxed is true.

CVE-2022-25174 / GHSA-g9fx-6j5c-grmw describes Jenkins Pipeline: Shared Groovy Libraries Plugin using the same checkout directories for distinct SCMs for Pipeline libraries, allowing users with Item/Configure permission to invoke arbitrary OS commands on the controller through crafted SCM contents. The reviewed exact source snapshot ff04fa68714d2cc277e8a87512461bdf3a39e186 is the vulnerable source snapshot used by the failed row. In that snapshot, SCMSourceRetriever.retrieve resolves the requested library version and calls doRetrieve(name, changelog, scm.build(...), ...). doRetrieve chooses the Jenkins controller workspace and constructs the library checkout directory with baseWorkspace.withSuffix(getFilePathSuffix() + "libs").child(name), so different SCMs sharing a library name share the same controller-side checkout directory. It then allocates that directory and invokes GenericSCMStep.checkout through node.createLauncher(listener), after which files are copied from the checkout into the Pipeline library target. The fixed commit ace0de3c2d691662021ea10306eeb407da6b6365 changes SCMSourceRetriever to compute checkoutDirName = LibraryRecord.directoryNameFor(scm.getKey()) and use child(checkoutDirName), while LibraryRecord adds HMACConfidentialKey-backed directoryNameFor(...). This binds the public advisory, exact vulnerable checkout, source-backed shared-library-name-to-controller-checkout path, and fixed SCM-key-derived checkout directory boundary.

CVE-2018-12036 affects OWASP Dependency-Check before 3.2.0 because crafted archive entry names can escape the intended extraction directory. In exact vulnerable checkout c3b5b3c0d7fe7283b4cd421149d6fb620476f67d, ArchiveAnalyzer.extractFiles opens zip/tar archives and dispatches them into extractArchive. ArchiveAnalyzer.extractArchive constructs new File(destination, entry.getName()) for every archive entry and extractAcceptedFile writes that file with FileOutputStream without canonicalizing the resulting path or checking that it remains under destination. The same pattern appears in ExtractionUtil.extractFiles for ZipInputStream and ExtractionUtil.extractArchive/extractFile for ArchiveInputStream: directory and file outputs are built from extractTo/destination plus entry.getName() and then created or written directly. A malicious entry such as ../outside can therefore target a path outside the temporary extraction directory. Version 3.2.0 adds destination.getCanonicalPath() checks in ArchiveAnalyzer for compressed outputs and archive entries, and in ExtractionUtil for ZipInputStream and ArchiveInputStream extraction, rejecting entries whose canonical output path does not start with the destination path.

CVE-2025-1948 describes Eclipse Jetty 12.0.0 through 12.0.16 accepting an excessively large HTTP/2 SETTINGS_MAX_HEADER_LIST_SIZE from a client and using it for HPACK response encoding, which can drive large ByteBuffer allocation and denial of service. The residual source snapshot 8414f79a9c476ecb78998c8ce88f0c5ae548f7e6 is itself the fix commit '#12690 cap MAX_HEADER_LIST_SIZE', so the reviewed-source evidence must bind the case to its parent prepatch checkout 487f7e710219b50f4b8e960444477fd1638ee4ce. In that prepatch checkout, HTTP2Session handles SettingsFrame.MAX_HEADER_LIST_SIZE and directly calls generator.getHpackEncoder().setMaxHeaderListSize(value) for remote/client settings. HpackEncoder.setMaxHeaderListSize assigns the provided value directly to _maxHeaderListSize. The fix commit changes the remote setting path to cap the encoder value with Math.min(value, hpackEncoder.getMaxHeaderListSize()) and changes setMaxHeaderListSize to fall back to the default for non-positive values; it also adds SettingsTest.testMaxHeaderListSizeCappedByClient to exercise the client-advertised oversized setting. These spans bind the vulnerable prepatch behavior to the exact parent of the public fix commit.

CVE-2023-33962 / GHSA-gwxv-jv83-6qjr describes a JStachio HTML escaping vulnerability fixed in 1.0.1: prior versions did not escape single quotes in HTML output, allowing XSS when escaped template variables are rendered into single-quoted HTML attributes. CVE-2014-3656 describes cross-site scripting in JBoss Keycloak login-status-iframe.html. The failed new-unified row uses exact source snapshot checkout 3b071b83aa0444749eba851fdbe0f2ed47932410, where integration/js/src/main/resources/login-status-iframe.html registers a message event handler. In that vulnerable snapshot, receiveMessage checks event.origin against the built origin, then directly mutates event.data by assigning loggedIn and session fields, reads the KEYCLOAK_SESSION cookie, and sends the same event.data object back with postMessage. This means message payload handling relies on a caller-supplied object crossing the postMessage boundary rather than a serialized data contract, matching the iframe XSS location named by NVD. Fix commit ce1fd8eedcaa814a647f42fdf45de718fa5bfc7f is titled using JSON.stringify(...) and JSON.parse(...); its patch changes the same file so receiveMessage parses event.data with JSON.parse, writes loggedIn/session to the parsed data object, and sends JSON.stringify(data) instead of event.data. This binds the advisory to source-backed postMessage intake, unsafe event.data mutation/echo, session-cookie propagation, and the JSON serialization fix in the named iframe resource.

CVE-2022-3782 / GHSA-g8q8-fggx-9r3q describes a Keycloak path traversal / redirect validation bypass via double URL encoding for clients using wildcard Valid Redirect URIs. The failed new-unified row uses exact source snapshot checkout cce8ee2b1ab7c925bfbb62d8f12a33e93d943040. In that checkout, AuthorizationEndpoint accepts GET/POST authorization parameters, AuthorizationEndpointChecker.checkRedirectUri reads request.getRedirectUriParam() and calls RedirectUtils.verifyRedirectUri. LogoutEndpoint similarly accepts post_logout_redirect_uri or legacy redirect_uri and calls RedirectUtils.verifyRedirectUri for client post-logout redirects. The shared RedirectUtils.verifyRedirectUri implementation creates a URI directly from the supplied redirectUri and normalizes it, then lower-cases the hostname and checks the still-encoded string against resolved valid redirects. Its wildcard matcher accepts a redirect when the request string starts with the configured wildcard prefix. There is no repeated decoding of the path component before normalization and wildcard matching, so double-encoded traversal segments can survive validation. Fix commit 1987c942f527b9f3bbf2a86ba71ba8ae0154ac37 adds decodeRedirectUri to RedirectUtils, invokes it before URI.create/normalize, decodes the redirect URL up to five times while preserving query and fragment, and adds regression tests for encoded and double-encoded ../ patterns. This binds the advisory to source-backed OIDC redirect parameter intake, missing multi-decode before redirect validation, wildcard prefix matching, and the production-source decode fix.

The exact vulnerable source snapshot fc3c61235fa30132123c17ed8702ff7b3a672fe9 is the direct parent of the backport fix commit cb167d4557dc75ad97e34c6d342f5c8019461365. The endpoint accepts code/error/error_description query parameters and on the error path calls forms.setError(error).createCode(). The pre-fix KeycloakSanitizerMethod sanitizes the immediate string only and lacks the decodeHtmlFull() loop added by the fix. CVE-2025-0604 / GHSA-2p82-5wwr-43cw describes Keycloak LDAP federation authentication bypass after reset credentials: an Active Directory user can reset a password and remain logged in without a fresh LDAP bind that would enforce disabled or expired AD account state. The failed new-unified row uses exact source snapshot checkout b70303f2932dabd5f462128b1dc8a3d2640799a2. In that checkout, ResetCredentialEmail.authenticate handles the reset-credential-email authenticator. When the user returns via the reset credentials action token, it detects DefaultActionTokenKey.ACTION_TOKEN_USER_ID, logs that it is skipping the reset email screen, immediately calls context.success(), and returns. The authenticator is not configurable, configuredFor always returns true, and there is no force-login behavior for federated users. ResetPassword then adds the UPDATE_PASSWORD required action and succeeds, and UpdatePassword updates the user password through user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...) followed by context.success(). This source path allows the reset-credentials flow to continue in the same authentication session after password update instead of forcing a fresh login path for LDAP/federated users. The production-source fix chain first adds a force-login option in commit 66a6248d519718d5b8c8800d52ffa46074ee9437, then commit 707a5568284c615393cc8d47857a2aae05dd2864 changes ResetCredentialEmail to use forceLogin(context.getAuthenticatorConfig(), user), changes the option default to only-federated, and implements forceLogin so federated users identified by non-local StorageId or federationLink get AuthenticationManager.END_AFTER_REQUIRED_ACTIONS set after reset credentials. This binds the advisory to source-backed reset credential action-token reauth, password update required action, missing federated-user forced re-login, and the LDAP/federated force-login production fix.

In that checkout, ResetCredentialEmail.authenticate handles the reset-credential-email authenticator. When the user returns via the reset credentials action token, it detects DefaultActionTokenKey.ACTION_TOKEN_USER_ID, logs that it is skipping the reset email screen, immediately calls context.success(), and returns. The authenticator is not configurable, configuredFor always returns true, and there is no force-login behavior for federated users. ResetPassword then adds the UPDATE_PASSWORD required action and succeeds, and UpdatePassword updates the user password through user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...) followed by context.success(). This source path allows the reset-credentials flow to continue in the same authentication session after password update instead of forcing a fresh login path for LDAP/federated users. The production-source fix chain first adds a force-login option in commit 66a6248d519718d5b8c8800d52ffa46074ee9437, then commit 707a5568284c615393cc8d47857a2aae05dd2864 changes ResetCredentialEmail to use forceLogin(context.getAuthenticatorConfig(), user), changes the option default to only-federated, and implements forceLogin so federated users identified by non-local StorageId or federationLink get AuthenticationManager.END_AFTER_REQUIRED_ACTIONS set after reset credentials. This binds the advisory to source-backed reset credential action-token reauth, password update required action, missing federated-user forced re-login, and the LDAP/federated force-login production fix.

CVE-2025-1391 / GHSA-gvgg-2r3r-53x7 describes improper authorization in the Keycloak organization mapper: organization claims can be included in tokens for a user that is not actually a member when username or email matches the organization domain pattern. The failed new-unified row uses exact source snapshot checkout 4b628610c42b7754d0b3f4a0283202a5dcaa9697. In that checkout, OrganizationAuthenticator.resolveOrganization resolves an organization from the user/domain and stores OrganizationModel.ORGANIZATION_ATTRIBUTE in the authentication session client note whenever an organization is resolved, without the later SSO-only guard. TokenManager.tryResolveDynamicClientScope accepts organization dynamic scopes by returning orgScope.toClientScope(name, user, session) without separately confirming that orgScope.resolveOrganizations(user, scopeParam, session) yields a membership. OrganizationMembershipMapper.setClaim then reads OrganizationModel.ORGANIZATION_ATTRIBUTE from the client session and directly converts that organization into a token claim. Its resolveValue method only skips null or disabled organizations; it does not require userSession.getUser() to be a member before returning the organization alias or attributes. Fix commit 6900d8da43087a265ee408d4db332587ebd62e2c changes the organization authenticator to set the organization client note on reauthentication only when isSSOAuthentication(authSession), passes the UserModel into OrganizationMembershipMapper.resolveValue and skips organizations where !o.isMember(user), and adds a TokenManager dynamic-scope membership check before returning an organization client scope. Backport commit 44f18467d5afc1db775572e8103cc8a1c300a5f0 applies the same source-level fix on the 26.0 line. This binds the advisory to source-backed organization selection/client note propagation, dynamic organization scope resolution, missing membership authorization in token claim mapping, and the production-source membership checks added by the fix.

CVE-2025-3501 / GHSA-HW58-3793-42GG describes a Keycloak hostname-verification flaw where setting the TLS hostname verifier policy to ANY causes truststore certificate verification for outgoing HTTPS/SMTP trust managers to be skipped. The failed new-unified row uses exact source snapshot checkout a78c951a5aeb820d01d2987397e24b3362c455f0. In that checkout, TruststoreOptions exposes the tls-hostname-verifier option with HostnameVerificationPolicy values, and JSSETruststoreConfigurator.getTrustManagers() checks getProvider().getPolicy() == HostnameVerificationPolicy.ANY before returning a custom X509TrustManager. That trust manager returns an empty accepted issuer array and leaves both checkClientTrusted and checkServerTrusted empty, bypassing the TrustManagerFactory path that would initialize from provider.getTruststore(). Fix commit 99ca24c832729075e04d8bc58666089268314272 removes this HostnameVerificationPolicy.ANY special branch from JSSETruststoreConfigurator and updates truststore option documentation to state that ANY should not be used in production. This binds the advisory to source-backed tls-hostname-verifier configuration, truststore provider policy selection, no-op X509TrustManager creation, and the production-source removal of the ANY trust-manager bypass.

CVE-2025-3910 allows circumventing administrator-required actions such as 2FA setup through login URL action manipulation. The vulnerable checkout passes kcAction != null into executeAction, treating any requested kc_action as action-initiated execution even when the first applicable required action is a different user/admin-required action. In the IGNORE path it removes the required action and records SUCCESS, allowing a required action to be skipped. PR #39351 fixes this by passing kcActionExecution only when kcAction equals the selected provider id and by no longer removing required actions on IGNORE.

CVE-2025-7365 / GHSA-xhpr-465j-7p9q describes a Keycloak phishing/account-linking flaw in the first broker login flow: after an authenticated attacker reaches the IdP account merge/review-profile path, the attacker can change the reviewed email address to a victim address and still use the Verify Existing Account By Email execution, causing a verification email that can link the external identity to the victim account. The failed new-unified row uses exact source snapshot checkout 1183157d862f9ccc66e1d6b36018e1aea6d49046. In that checkout, AbstractIdentityProvider defines only UPDATE_PROFILE_EMAIL_CHANGED for the review page, IdpReviewProfileAuthenticator.processAction records the email-changed note when the review profile email attribute changes, and IdpConfirmLinkAuthenticator lets the user choose updateProfile before linkAccount. IdpEmailVerificationAuthenticator.authenticateImpl then proceeds from SMTP availability directly to existing-user lookup and sendVerifyEmail unless the VERIFY_ACCOUNT_IDP_USERNAME auth note already matches the broker username; it does not check the review-profile changed email note, and there is no username-changed note at all. sendVerifyEmail builds an IdpVerifyAccountLinkActionToken for the existing user email and sends the confirm identity broker link message. Fix commit b5d6c8c4021717e26eccfe041dba4fbc81e5f186 records username changes, checks UPDATE_PROFILE_USERNAME_CHANGED or UPDATE_PROFILE_EMAIL_CHANGED before email verification, calls context.attempted() when either changed, and hides the review button unless the review execution previously succeeded. This binds the advisory to source-backed first-broker-login review-profile mutation, missing changed-profile gate before email verification, verification-token email dispatch, and the production-source fix that disables email verification after manual review changes.

CVE-2025-7784 / GHSA-27gp-8389-hm4w describes a Keycloak FGAPv2 privilege escalation where an administrator with manage-users style authority could escalate to realm-admin because fine-grained admin permission checks around admin role mappings did not require a server administrator. The exact vulnerable source snapshot 73e5f4bead7840f19210aaabcbd1a00895d46929 is the Keycloak 26.2.5 release tag in the affected range before 26.2.6. The fixed source snapshot 51bd67030d264a6f001de425ce558fad55970336 is the Keycloak 26.2.6 release tag, whose release notes state that admin role mappings are restricted to server administrators. In the vulnerable checkout, UserResource exposes /role-mappings for a user with manageCheck bound to auth.users().requireMapRoles(user). RoleMapperResource.addRealmRoleMappings first requires that manage permission, then for each requested realm role calls auth.roles().requireMapRole(roleModel) before granting the role. RolePermissionsV2.canMapRole returns checkAdminRoles(role) for admins with MANAGE_USERS and also combines hasPermission(...MAP_ROLE_SCOPE) with checkAdminRoles(role). The inherited checkAdminRoles accepts admin roles in the realm-management client by checking similar realm-level permissions such as root.users().canManage() for MANAGE_USERS, rather than requiring a master-realm server admin. The 26.2.6 fix adds hasMasterAdminRole() and denies AdminRoles.ALL_ROLES mapping in canMapRole/canMapComposite unless the acting admin has the master realm admin role; it also removes the old checkAdminRoles gating from the FGAPv2 canMapRole return path. This binds the advisory to source-backed role mapping entrypoints and the fixed permission boundary.

The failed new-unified row uses exact source snapshot checkout 796c74f4244cacd90d99393640ccaad0c72f8893. In that checkout, Copy.copyDirectoryFromPod verifies tar availability, executes `tar cz - <srcPath> | base64` inside the target pod, decodes the process output through Base64InputStream, GzipCompressorInputStream, and TarArchiveInputStream, iterates each ArchiveEntry, and constructs the local destination with new File(destination.toFile(), entry.getName()). It then creates directories and writes file bytes without normalizing the archive entry name or ensuring the resulting path remains under the destination directory. Fix commit eb2cfe945c1492503b086606734530550630d31f adds commons-io FilenameUtils and changes this construction to FilenameUtils.normalize(entry.getName()), rejecting null normalized names before building the destination File. This binds the advisory to source-backed pod tar archive intake, archive-entry name trust, destination path construction, and the production-source normalization fix.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2016-10006 / GHSA-683w-6h9j-57wq describes an AntiSamy XSS bypass before 1.5.5 where a specially crafted tag that supports style with active content can bypass library protections. The upstream issue is titled Style validation in attributes is not properly handled, and fix commit 7313931dc3c0d1377b010f07faef2063dd359a36 is titled Updated for proper style tag validation, stating that it validated style tag attributes to fix style tag XSS in MagicSAXFilter.java. The failed new-unified row uses exact source snapshot checkout 8bebe1eb2ec1ac23e34111e9d06024d7dab7fa25, immediately before that fix. In that checkout, MagicSAXFilter.startElement detects a validate-action style tag and immediately pushes Ops.CSS, initializes cssContent, and stores cssAttributes = attributes. This branch bypasses the generic attribute validation loop that scans inline style attributes, checks allowed attributes and expressions, and builds validattributes. Later, characters() records only style element text while in Ops.CSS, and endElement() scans cssContent with CssScanner but emits the style element using super.startElement(element, cssAttributes, ...), preserving the original unvalidated style tag attributes. The fix moves style tag CSS mode after the generic attribute validation and assigns cssAttributes = validattributes, binding the advisory to source-backed style-tag attribute bypass, CSS content scanning, unvalidated attribute writeback, and the production-source validation fix.

CVE-2017-14735 describes OWASP AntiSamy before 1.5.7 allowing XSS through HTML5 entities, demonstrated by using : to construct a javascript: URL. The v1.5.7 tag commit e76f02a77afb4e43b897f13d17b5bc1260b8afde is titled Release version 1.5.7 and its message references Issue #10 with policy updates sensitive to the html5 colon entity. Its parent c48ed190a8e8e374444588ef43bb058dced3b93f is the reviewed prepatch checkout. In that prepatch checkout, antisamy.xml defines onsiteURL as a permissive character-class expression that includes ampersand and semicolon, and href accepts onsiteURL before offsiteURL. The existing tests reject literal javascript: and numeric-entity javascript payloads, but the later fix adds a new issue10 regression asserting that javascript:alert(1) is removed in both DOM and SAX modes. The fix changes all bundled onsiteURL regexes to a negative lookahead that rejects &colon and adds anchoredURL separately, binding the vulnerable prepatch policy behavior to the patched 1.5.7 release.

CVE-2022-28367 / GHSA-3pqg-4rqg-pg9g describes an AntiSamy XSS issue where STYLE tag content could be smuggled because the DOM scanner did not properly encode or sanitize CSS content split across multiple child nodes. In the exact vulnerable source snapshot b7c151112dd19928e700ee48639942fd1079d1e3, AntiSamyDOMScanner.actionValidate special-cases style tags and delegates them to processStyleTag(), but processStyleTag() reads only ele.getFirstChild(), scans firstChild.getNodeValue() with CssScanner, and writes the cleaned CSS back only to that first child. Additional child nodes under the style element are neither included in toScan nor removed after cleaning, so attacker-controlled markup split into later STYLE children can survive the CSS scanner path. The fixing commit 0199e7e194dba5e7d7197703f43ebe22401e61ae is titled "Support multiple children handling on style tags" and changes processStyleTag() to concatenate textContent from every child node, scan the combined CSS text, set the cleaned result on the first child, and remove all remaining child nodes; the added test covers a smuggled input containing <style><script>alert(1)</script></style>@import.

CVE-2022-29577 / GHSA-vp37-2f9p-3vr3 describes an AntiSamy XSS issue that exists because of an incomplete fix for CVE-2022-28367. The failed new-unified row uses exact source snapshot checkout b6e76de85a07549f2c97941437dd73430d7287a8. In that checkout, AntiSamyDOMScanner.actionValidate routes style tags to processStyleTag before normal child processing. processStyleTag concatenates textContent from every child node and scans the combined CSS with CssScanner, then writes the clean CSS into the first child. However, it removes remaining child nodes with a forward loop over ele.getChildNodes().getLength() starting at index 1 while the NodeList is updated by each removal. That live-list forward deletion can skip later child nodes, leaving attacker-controlled smuggled nodes under the style element after CSS cleaning. Fix commit 32e273507da0e964b58c50fd8a4c94c9d9363af0 stores the original childNodesCount and removes extra children from childNodesCount - 1 down to 1, explicitly noting the reverse order is needed because the list updates on the fly. The added regression tests cover smuggled input containing select/style/input and assert that DOM and SAX output do not contain the injected input. This binds the advisory to source-backed style-tag dispatch, multi-child CSS text aggregation, first-child clean writeback, live NodeList forward-removal skip, and the production-source reverse-removal fix.

CVE-2025-27508 / GHSA-hw43-fcmm-3m5g describes Emissary exposing ChecksumCalculator for hashing and checksum generation with weak or non-cryptographic algorithms such as SHA-1 and CRC32, creating risk if the utility is used for security-sensitive guarantees. The failed new-unified row uses exact source snapshot checkout ff9fed1d5910ca1879a290b78045ec991a93cb2e. In that checkout, src/main/java/emissary/kff/ChecksumCalculator.java declares a public ChecksumCalculator class documented only as a utility for checksums and message digests. Its public no-argument constructor initializes SHA-1 and enables CRC32 by default, and other public constructors accept arbitrary algorithm names or collections, with explicit support for CRC32 and SSDEEP. The digest(byte[]) and digest(SeekableByteChannelFactory) methods compute configured MessageDigest values, CRC32, and ssdeep and place them into ChecksumResults. Fix commit da3a81a8977577597ff2a944820a5ae4e9762368 makes the class and its constructors package-private, documents that it is for KFF/document similarity only, and states it is not meant to provide cryptographically secure hashes or checksums. This binds the advisory to source-backed public API exposure, weak/default algorithm selection, digest/checksum output, and the production-source visibility and documentation fix.

CVE-2025-25193 / GHSA-389x-839f-4rhx describes a Netty denial of service on Windows where the previous large-file mitigation was incomplete because null bytes were not counted against the input limit. The failed new-unified row uses exact source snapshot checkout f844d78e4e23182610a24576d225de933f90f92e, which is the direct parent of fix commit d1fbda62d3a47835d3fb35db8bd42ecc205a5386. In that checkout, BoundedInputStream stores maxBytesRead and numRead, but its single-byte read() increments numRead only when the returned byte value is greater than zero. Java InputStream.read returns byte values from 0 to 255 and -1 for EOF, so a valid 0x00 byte is read but not counted. The bulk read(byte[], off, len) path similarly increments numRead only when the return count is greater than zero, and both paths call checkMaxBytesRead after the read, allowing the zero-byte stream case named by the advisory to bypass the bound. The existing vulnerable test only uses random bytes and has no deterministic all-byte/null-byte coverage. Fix commit d1fbda62d3a47835d3fb35db8bd42ecc205a5386 changes both read paths to count every value except -1, removes the post-read check so reads are truncated to the limit before failing on the next read, and adds deterministic testBoundEnforced256 coverage for all byte values including 0x00. This binds the advisory to source-backed BoundedInputStream byte-counting behavior, the null-byte bound bypass, and the production-source fix that counts valid zero bytes.

CVE-2025-29908 / GHSA-HQQC-JR88-P6X2 describes a Netty QUIC hash-collision denial of service where remote attackers can send packets with colliding Source Connection IDs and drive excessive CPU through the connection-id map. The failed new-unified row uses exact source snapshot checkout dca355aa8a1f63dfaf6aa2fe88734e4bd5314c14. In that checkout, QuicheQuicCodec stores connection IDs in a plain HashMap keyed by ByteBuffer. Incoming DatagramPacket content is parsed by QuicHeaderParser, which passes parsed SCID and DCID into quicPacketRead. The codec then tracks active channel source connection IDs with direct HashMap get, put, remove, clear, and add/remove mapping operations. New and retired source connection IDs returned by a channel are inserted into or removed from the same HashMap. Fix commit e059bd9b78723f8b035e0c547e42ce263f03461c replaces the plain HashMap with ConnectionIdChannelMap backed by SipHash 1-3 using random keys, explicitly to prevent connection-id hash collision attacks. This binds the advisory to source-backed datagram-to-header processing, SCID/DCID channel dispatch, vulnerable ByteBuffer HashMap storage, source-connection-id mapping updates, and the production-source SipHash map fix.

CVE-2025-27497 / GHSA-93qr-h8pr-4593 describes an OpenDJ denial of service where an LDAP search with alias dereferencing set to always against an alias loop can make the server stop responding to future LDAP requests. The failed new-unified row uses exact source snapshot checkout 688a9ffc80d3c6c21c9cf1b89b1a6d8ed7d0cc1d, which is the direct parent of fix commit 08aee4724608e4a32baa3c7d7499ec913a275aaf. In that checkout, LocalBackendSearchOperation.processSearch checks dereference policies ALWAYS, FINDING_BASE, and IN_SEARCHING for subtree searches, loads the base entry, and if it is an alias directly replaces baseDN with baseEntry.getAliasedDN() and recursively calls processSearch. There is no set of already dereferenced DNs and no recursion guard, so two alias entries pointing to each other can cause unbounded recursive search processing. The pre-fix AliasTestCase covers normal alias dereferencing but does not include recursive alias entries. Fix commit 08aee4724608e4a32baa3c7d7499ec913a275aaf adds a dereferencingDNs HashSet, checks whether the next aliased DN has already been seen before recursion, removes the DN after recursive processing, catches StackOverflowError as an exception, and adds tests for recursive aliases and deep stack-overflow cases. This binds the advisory to source-backed LDAP alias dereference policy handling, unguarded baseDN recursion, missing recursion detection, and the production-source visited-DN fix.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2025-46096 describes a Solon v3.1.2 solon-faas-luffy directory traversal issue that can lead to XSS when attacker-controlled paths reach the Luffy file loader. The failed new-unified row uses exact source snapshot checkout 4fdbc8f37e3e752d4b267b486116399597ea56b4, which is before fixed version v3.2.0 and before fix commit 49a3bf95fdcf050829843004b65a2b336ca6ddff. In that checkout, LuffyHandler.handle obtains the request path from ctx.pathNew() and passes it through handleDo to JtRun.fileGet. JtRun.fileGet delegates to the JtExecutorAdapter backed by JtFunctionLoaderManager, whose fileGet iterates registered JtFunctionLoader instances and calls each loader with the same path. JtFunctionLoaderFile.fileGet accepts the path without any ../ or ..\ rejection, calls fileBuildDo, and fileBuildDo constructs new File(_baseDir, path) directly. Because the default base directory is ./luffy/ and the pre-fix path is not normalized or constrained before new File(_baseDir, path), traversal segments can escape the intended Luffy repository and load arbitrary existing files as AFileModel content, which LuffyHandler then exposes to the executor path. Fix commit 49a3bf95fdcf050829843004b65a2b336ca6ddff adds an entry guard in JtFunctionLoaderFile.fileGet that returns null when path contains ../ or ..\, explicitly preventing traversal into or out of the repository. This binds the advisory to source-backed request path handling, unguarded external file loader path resolution, file content loading, and the production-source traversal guard added by the fix.

CVE-2020-13973 / GHSA-g8jj-899q-8x3j describes XSS in OWASP json-sanitizer before 1.2.1 when sanitized JSON is embedded in an HTML script element. In the reviewed exact source snapshot bb41f80ad575cb90ea6535976d7c17accb4b4c87, the class-level output contract says the sanitizer output avoids </script and ]]> for script/CDATA embedding, and sanitize(String) routes all input through sanitizeString(). The vulnerable sanitizeString() embedding logic only escapes the slash in </script-like substrings and escapes ]]>; it does not escape HTML parser state-changing sequences <script, <!--, or --> described by the advisory. PR #20 changes that same embedding block to operate on '<' and '>' characters, replacing '<' with \u003c for <!--, <script, and </script patterns and replacing '>' with \u003e for -->, and adds regression tests testHtmlParserStateChanges for <script, <!--, -->, and <!--<script>. These source spans bind the public XSS issue to the sanitizer entrypoint, documented HTML/script embedding contract, vulnerable incomplete embedding filter, and the output mutation helpers used by the fix.

CVE-2022-37422 / GHSA-h28c-453m-h9xm describes Payara before 5.2022.3 allowing path traversal for web applications deployed at the default ROOT context. In that checkout, StandardContextValve.preInvoke obtains the request path, calls normalize, and blocks direct access only when the normalized path is null or starts with /META-INF/ or /WEB-INF/. CVE-2016-9177 describes a directory traversal / arbitrary file read issue in Spark 2.5 static file serving, allowing remote attackers to read files via dot-dot URI traversal. The reviewed exact source snapshot ce57dfb949ed183405f75dee8cf3262b45c9b3b5 is the failed row's vulnerable 2.5.1 source snapshot. In that snapshot, MatcherFilter invokes StaticFilesConfiguration.consume before route matching. consumeWithFileResourceHandlers calls each ClassPathResourceHandler or ExternalResourceHandler with the servlet request; AbstractResourceHandler builds pathInContext from servletPath and pathInfo; the concrete handlers canonicalize URI path segments, append that path to the configured base resource, create ClassPathResource or ExternalResource, and return it if readable. StaticFilesConfiguration then streams resource.getInputStream() to the HTTP response. The 2.5.2 fix commit 26b57d0, titled Fix for #700 - Arbitrary File Read Vulnerability, adds DirectoryTraversal checks in both ClassPathResourceHandler and ExternalResourceHandler to ensure the resolved resource path still starts with the configured static-files folder before it can be served, and wraps consume() to log and reject traversal detection. This binds the public advisory, exact vulnerable checkout, source-backed static-file request-to-read path, and fix-bound base-prefix containment guard.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2025-47293 / GHSA-qpj9-qcwx-8jv2 describes PowSyBl Core XML Reader allowing XXE and SSRF before the v6.7.2 fix. The failed new-unified row uses exact source snapshot checkout 72f79dec6d4292f892fbddd68a19c67935c7d81f. In that checkout, commons XmlReader memoizes XMLInputFactory.newInstance() and constructs XMLStreamReader directly from supplied input streams without disabling DTD or external entities. IIDM XMLImporter and CGMES NamespaceReader use the same default XMLInputFactory.newInstance pattern, while FullModel only disables ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD and ACCESS_EXTERNAL_SCHEMA and still lacks the broader DTD, entity, and secure-processing controls added by the fix. Fix commit e6c7c4997ae8758b54a2f23ce1a499e25113acdc, titled Secure XMLReader by adding security properties and included in v6.7.2, centralizes XML factory creation in XmlUtil.getXMLInputFactory(), disables SUPPORT_DTD, IS_SUPPORTING_EXTERNAL_ENTITIES, IS_REPLACING_ENTITY_REFERENCES, external DTD/schema/stylesheet access, and enables secure processing; it also replaces the vulnerable reader call sites and adds XXE regression tests that verify secret file content is not leaked. This binds the advisory to source-backed XML parser construction, unsafe StAX defaults in shared readers/importers, and the production-source secure XML factory fix.

CVE-2025-47771 describes PowSyBl Core allowing deserialization of untrusted SparseMatrix data before the v6.7.2 fix. The failed new-unified row uses exact source snapshot checkout d8398f689a5ccd505bd62eee2bd6670a29133110. In that checkout, SparseMatrix is Serializable, write(OutputStream) serializes the matrix with ObjectOutputStream.writeObject(this), and read(InputStream) constructs a plain ObjectInputStream over caller-supplied bytes and immediately casts objectInputStream.readObject() to SparseMatrix. The code has no ObjectInputFilter and no pre-deserialization class allowlist, so an attacker-controlled serialized stream can instantiate arbitrary gadget classes before the cast. Fix commit 8ed16ce41683c4aef5f6aa1dd5ae8642aa5ed2bd, titled Check object type at SparseMatrix deserialization and included in v6.7.2, adds an ALLOWED_CLASSES set for SparseMatrix and its primitive/trove backing types, installs ObjectInputFilter.allowFilter before readObject(), and adds SparseMatrixDeserializationTest where a malicious readObject payload attempts to create an rce file and is rejected. This binds the advisory to source-backed Java object deserialization in SparseMatrix.read and the production-source object filter fix.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2018-1000129 affects Jolokia 1.3.7/1.4.0 HTTP servlet responses because the response MIME type can be controlled with the mimeType request parameter. In exact source snapshot 10727cab59a8fc2ae053bec6b2f26f48f1c4245c, AgentServlet.getMimeType reads pReq.getParameter(ConfigKey.MIME_TYPE.getKeyValue()) and returns that value directly when present. AgentServlet.sendResponse then calls setContentType with callback != null ? text/javascript : getMimeType(pReq), sets the status to OK, disables caching, and writes the JSON/JSONP response bytes to the servlet output stream. The GET and POST servlet request handlers pass the request parameter map into HttpRequestHandler, so externally supplied requests can carry both operation parameters and mimeType. The fixing commit 5895d5c137c335e6b473e9dcb9baf748851bbc5f removes the direct getMimeType helper, routes response type selection through MimeTypeUtil.getResponseMimeType, sanitizes request/default MIME values to only application/json or text/plain with invalid values falling back to text/plain, and validates JSONP callback names before handling the request.

CVE-2025-27136 / GHSA-G6WM-2V64-WQ36 describes an XML External Entity injection in LocalS3's CreateBucketConfiguration endpoint. In the exact vulnerable source snapshot 009901882be8b543e85b67c5ec2e9f30d83d62ef, LocalS3.createServiceFactory() constructs the service-wide XmlMapper from a WstxInputFactory that only disables namespace awareness; XmlUtils uses the same insecure WstxInputFactory pattern. CreateBucketController.handle() reads the request body through this XmlMapper into CreateBucketConfiguration, then stores createBucketConfig.getLocationConstraint() as the bucket region through BucketService.createBucket(). GetBucketLocationController later serializes the stored region in the bucket location response. The fixing commit d6ed756ceb30c1eb9d4263321ac683d734f8836f is explicitly titled 'fix XML External Entity (XXE) Injection (#172)' and adds XMLInputFactory.SUPPORT_DTD=false and XMLInputFactory.IS_SUPPORTING_EXTERNAL_ENTITIES=false to both LocalS3.createServiceFactory() and XmlUtils, directly disabling the vulnerable DTD/external-entity processing path.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2025-2240 / GHSA-gfh6-3pqw-x2j4 describes a SmallRye Fault Tolerance out-of-memory issue externally triggerable through metrics collection, where repeated creation of Guard or TypedGuard objects without an explicit description causes new metric objects to accumulate. The failed new-unified row uses exact source snapshot checkout 8da7dae36f195608291687793ca9f12fd9567d93. In that checkout, Guard.Builder and TypedGuard.Builder document that a random UUID is used when no description is set, and the implementation initializes description with UUID.randomUUID().toString() in both GuardImpl.BuilderImpl and TypedGuardImpl.BuilderImpl. buildStrategy then creates a BasicMeteredOperationImpl using that description and wraps the strategy in DelegatingMetricsCollector whenever metrics are enabled. BasicMeteredOperationImpl.cacheKey() returns name, while DelegatingMetricsCollector and the concrete MicroProfile, Micrometer, OpenTelemetry, and compound metrics providers all cache MetricsCollector or MetricsRecorder instances by the operation or operation cache key. Therefore every newly created undescribed Guard or TypedGuard can introduce a fresh random metrics method tag/cache key that remains retained by the metrics maps, matching the advisory memory growth condition during repeated metrics endpoint access. Fix commit e8bcad3d5e8bbac0a3219bd5c13661adf6ed6bbb, titled fix memory leak in metrics, adds a descriptionSet flag, extends MeteredOperation with enabled(), passes descriptionSet into BasicMeteredOperationImpl, and changes DelegatingMetricsCollector to bypass metrics caching/emission when operation.enabled() is false. The fix message explicitly states that random UUID metric method tags were held in memory and that no metrics are emitted when no description is set.

CVE-2025-24789 / GHSA-7hpq-3g6w-pvhf describes a Snowflake JDBC Windows EXTERNALBROWSER authentication issue where the driver could open the browser through an untrusted search path; a local attacker with write access to a directory in %PATH% could escalate privileges to the user running the vulnerable JDBC driver. The local NVD/vulndb entry states the issue affects versions 3.2.3 through 3.21.0 on Windows and is fixed in 3.22.0, with patch URL commit 4f01bb8f9b708c71e7a2111c87371dbfc1d53dd6. The exact source snapshot 9e1a5acf12406b16c4780ca013f4c4db48b74b59 is a 3.21.1-SNAPSHOT checkout immediately before the SNOW-1708383 fix commit. In that vulnerable checkout, SessionUtil.newSession routes EXTERNALBROWSER authentication to SessionUtilExternalBrowser.authenticate(), authenticate obtains an SSO or console login URL and calls handlers.openBrowser(...), and DefaultAuthExternalBrowserHandlers.openBrowser validates the URL but, when AWT Desktop is unsupported, distinguishes only Mac from all other operating systems. Windows therefore falls into the generic else branch that executes a command string, runtime.exec("xdg-open " + ssoUrl), rather than invoking a Windows browser handler by a Windows-specific argument vector. The fixing commit imports java.awt.Desktop, checks Desktop.Action.BROWSE support, and adds a Windows-specific branch runtime.exec(new String[] {"rundll32", "url.dll,FileProtocolHandler", ssoUrl}); this is the source-level change corresponding to the untrusted-search-path advisory.

CVE-2025-24790 / GHSA-33g6-495w-v8j2 describes Snowflake JDBC temporary credential caching on Linux writing temporary credentials to a world-readable local file when EXTERNALBROWSER or USERNAME_PASSWORD_MFA authentication is used with temporary credential caching enabled. In the exact vulnerable source snapshot 3236d9840c61cdffa7093c631539523b9d1d6836, SessionUtil enables and uses CLIENT_STORE_TEMPORARY_CREDENTIAL to read cached ID tokens before a session and write returned ID/MFA tokens after login. On Linux, SecureStorageLinuxManager stores those credentials in temporary_credential.json via FileCacheManager. FileCacheManager builds ~/.cache/snowflake/temporary_credential.json and creates it with File.createNewFile(), then only logs/warns about broad permissions via FileUtil.logFileUsage; reads and writes likewise only log access and do not reject group/other readable files. Fix commit 9e1a5acf12406b16c4780ca013f4c4db48b74b59 creates cache files with POSIX OWNER_READ/OWNER_WRITE permissions on non-Windows systems, adds read/write/override permission checks, adds owner checks for reads, and adds FileCacheManagerTest cases that reject group/other readable, writable, or executable permissions.

In that checkout, SnowflakeFileTransferAgent.parseCommandInGS sends the GET/PUT command to GS, receives a JsonNode response, and immediately executes logger.debug("Response: {}", jsonNode.toString()). The same response is later parsed by parseCommand(), which reads data.encryptionMaterial through initEncryptionMaterial() / getEncryptionMaterial() and converts it into RemoteStoreFileEncryptionMaterial for upload and download flows. EncryptionProvider and GcmEncryptionProvider then consume encMat.getQueryStageMasterKey() as the key-encryption key for file encryption and decryption, confirming that the logged JSON field carries the sensitive client-side encryption material described by the advisory. The existing SecretDetector.maskSecrets() in the vulnerable checkout filtered access tokens, passwords, SAS tokens, AWS keys, and OAuth tokens, but did not filter encryptionMaterial JSON. Fix commit ef81582ce2f1dbc3c8794a696c94f4fe65fad507, titled SNOW-1660591 Remove sensitive encryption info when logging, imports SecretDetector in SnowflakeFileTransferAgent, changes the DEBUG response log to SecretDetector.maskSecrets(jsonNode.toString()), and adds SecretDetector.filterEncryptionMaterial() with a pattern for the encryptionMaterial object plus a regression test. provenance.rationale: CVE-2018-1260 / GHSA-rrpm-pj7p-7j9q describes remote code execution in Spring Security OAuth before fixed releases including 2.3.3.RELEASE. The failed new-unified row uses exact source snapshot checkout 97e39dde7e88aae802be98de084a382886ca4255, which is the 2.3.2.RELEASE snapshot immediately before the 2.3.3.RELEASE fix line. In that checkout, AuthorizationEndpoint creates an AuthorizationRequest from user request parameters, stores it in the model, and forwards to the default user approval page. getUserApprovalPageResponse merges userApprovalHandler.getUserApprovalRequest into the model; DefaultUserApprovalHandler includes the original authorization request parameters. WhitelabelApprovalEndpoint then creates an approval-page template, injects the model/request scopes directly into SCOPE by string replacement without HTML escaping, and returns a ModelAndView backed by SpelView. SpelView masks literal ${ markers in its template, then PropertyPlaceholderHelper resolves placeholders by parsing each placeholder name with SpelExpressionParser and evaluating the expression against a StandardEvaluationContext over the model. This means a malicious scope such as ${T(java.lang.Runtime).getRuntime().exec(...)} can be introduced into the approval page template and evaluated as SpEL during rendering. Fix commit adb1e6d19c681f394c9513799b81b527b0cb007c, titled Remove SpelView in WhitelabelApprovalEndpoint and fixing gh-1340, deletes SpelView, rewrites WhitelabelApprovalEndpoint to build a static View that appends already-rendered content, escapes clientId, csrf fields, and scopes with HtmlUtils.htmlEscape, changes WhitelabelErrorEndpoint away from SpelView, and adds a regression test testApprovalPageWithSuspectScope using the payload ${T(java.lang.Runtime).getRuntime().exec("cd ..")} to ensure the raw scope is not present and is escaped instead. This binds the advisory to source-backed SpEL evaluation of user-controlled approval-page content and the production fix that removes the SpEL renderer.

CVE-2020-5405 is a Spring Cloud Config Server directory traversal issue in affected 2.1.x versions before 2.1.7 and 2.2.x versions before 2.2.2. The reviewed checkout is spring-cloud-config-server 2.1.6.RELEASE. In this source, ResourceController derives the tail path directly from the request URL and passes it to ResourceRepository.findOne, while resolveLabel() converts the (_) placeholder back to slash for label-based search locations. NativeEnvironmentRepository.getLocations() substitutes the attacker-controlled normalized label into configured search locations. GenericResourceRepository.findOne() iterates those locations and calls createRelative(local); it validates the requested local path but does not reject traversal in the resolved search location. The 2.1.7/2.2.2 fixed source adds isInvalidEncodedLocation(location) and isInvalidLocation(location) checks before resolving resources, rejecting encoded or decoded locations containing .. .

CVE-2020-5410 / GHSA-32xf-jwmv-9hf3 describes a directory traversal issue in Spring Cloud Config Server where a crafted URL can cause the server to return a resource outside the configured search locations. The failed new-unified row uses exact source snapshot checkout 91843a9ddc7489275b679568bfce1e4c37af71e1, which is upstream tag v2.1.8.RELEASE and falls in the affected 2.1.0 through 2.1.8 range. In that checkout, ResourceController exposes wildcard resource endpoints, extracts the trailing request path from the servlet path, and passes it directly to ResourceRepository.findOne() for text and binary responses. The default ResourceRepository bean is GenericResourceRepository backed by a SearchPathLocator such as NativeEnvironmentRepository, whose getLocations() supplies file/classpath search locations. GenericResourceRepository.findOne() only rejects obvious invalid locations and paths through PathUtils, then resolves each user-controlled local path with resourceLoader.getResource(location).createRelative(local). If the resulting Resource exists and is readable, the old code returns it without checking that the resolved URL remains under the original location or any allowed search location. PathUtils in v2.1.8.RELEASE rejects WEB-INF/META-INF, URL-looking paths, and paths that still contain ../ after cleaning, but it has no post-resolution containment check for an absolute or encoded path that Resource.createRelative() resolves outside file:./. Fix commit 03eaadc25323d8c8c89f528e8585033ed90c50f6, titled Verifies resources are in allowed locations, is contained in v2.1.9.RELEASE. It first materializes allowed location Resources, changes GenericResourceRepository to call PathUtils.checkResource(file, location, locationResources) before returning a readable file, and adds PathUtils.isResourceUnderLocation() to require the resolved resource to be under the current or allowed locations. The regression test invalidPathEncodedSlash builds an encoded absolute path to src/test/resources/ssh/key while searchLocations is file:./ and expects NoSuchResourceException plus the new warning that the resource is neither under the current location nor under allowed locations. This binds the advisory to source-backed external resource resolution and the production containment fix.

CVE-2022-22947 describes Spring Cloud Gateway code injection when the Gateway Actuator endpoint is enabled, exposed, and unsecured. In the reviewed exact source snapshot da0f9014bcc9131d8f15141be74011b89a01420f, AbstractGatewayControllerEndpoint.save() accepts a POSTed RouteDefinition body and saves it through RouteDefinitionWriter after only checking that referenced filter and predicate names exist. InMemoryRouteDefinitionRepository.save() stores that route definition. RouteDefinitionRouteLocator later converts stored route definitions into executable routes, binding attacker-supplied filter and predicate argument maps through ConfigurationService. ShortcutConfigurable.normalize() calls getValue() on each shortcut argument, and getValue() treats values wrapped in #{...} as SpEL templates, creates a StandardEvaluationContext with a BeanFactoryResolver, parses the expression, and evaluates it. That route from actuator-supplied route arguments to unrestricted SpEL evaluation matches the public arbitrary code injection advisory. The fixed 3.0.7 ShortcutConfigurable source changes the same getValue() block to instantiate GatewayEvaluationContext instead of StandardEvaluationContext, constraining evaluation while leaving the actuator route-save and route-conversion shape intact.

CVE-2022-22965 / Spring4Shell describes unsafe data binding in Spring Framework where request-bound property paths can reach dangerous ClassLoader-related properties such as class.module.classLoader under specific servlet container and JDK conditions. In the reviewed exact source snapshot 925b07826067d57a8a057837a1b5973cb6fad186, DataBinder.bind() accepts PropertyValues, doBind() applies allowed/required filtering, and applyPropertyValues() sends all remaining values to the bean property accessor. BeanPropertyBindingResult creates a BeanWrapper for the target object, BeanWrapperImpl resolves local property handlers from CachedIntrospectionResults, and AbstractNestablePropertyAccessor recursively navigates nested property paths before setting values. CachedIntrospectionResults in 5.2.19 only filters classLoader and protectionDomain when the introspected beanClass is exactly Class.class, so it does not filter the class.module descriptor on Class nor ClassLoader-typed descriptors reached through module.classLoader. Public fix commit 996f701a1916d10202c1d0d281f06ab1f2e1117e / 5.2.20 changes this same descriptor filtering logic to allow only Class name variants and skip any descriptor whose property type is assignable to ClassLoader or ProtectionDomain. These reviewed source spans bind the external Spring4Shell issue to the DataBinder request-parameter binding flow, nested BeanWrapper traversal, descriptor exposure, and the fixed ClassLoader/ProtectionDomain filtering point.
