CVE-2025-41234 / GHSA-6r3c-xf4w-jxjm describes a reflected file download issue when an application creates a Content-Disposition header with org.springframework.http.ContentDisposition, sets the filename through ContentDisposition.Builder#filename(String, Charset), uses a non-ASCII charset, derives the filename from unsanitized user input, and serves attacker-controlled downloaded content. The failed new-unified row uses exact source snapshot checkout e86dc9ad95204e71f93e1338cb7ccf379e3fbd70. GitHub compare shows this exact 6.2.x checkout is one commit before f0e7b42704e6b33958f242d91bd690d6ef7ada9c and two commits before v6.2.8, the OSS fixed release. In the exact checkout, Builder.filename(String, Charset) stores both user-provided filename and charset, build() passes them into ContentDisposition, and toString() emits a Content-Disposition header. For non-ASCII charsets, toString() appends a quoted filename parameter containing encodeQuotedPrintableFilename(filename, charset), then appends the RFC 5987 filename* parameter. encodeQuotedPrintableFilename iterates over filename bytes and copies any byte considered PRINTABLE directly into the RFC 2047 Q-encoded value. The vulnerable static PRINTABLE set includes all bytes 33 through 126 except '=', '?', and '_'; it does not exclude double quote (byte 34). Therefore a user-controlled filename beginning with a double quote and containing non-ASCII content can leave the quote unencoded inside the quoted filename parameter, matching the advisory's Content-Disposition reflected file download condition. ASCII filename(String) paths use encodeQuotedPairs(), which escapes quotes, and the exact checkout has tests for ASCII quote escaping, but lacks the UTF-8 quoted filename regression. Fix commit f0e7b42704e6b33958f242d91bd690d6ef7ada9c, titled Encode non-printable character in Content-Disposition parameter, changes ContentDisposition.PRINTABLE to set byte 34 false and adds a regression test formatWithUtf8FilenameWithQuotes expecting the quote to be encoded as =22 in the RFC 2047 filename and %22 in filename*. The related fd68ea6f commit applies the same fix on the other release line. This binds the advisory to source-backed ContentDisposition filename header formatting and the production fix that encodes double quote in non-ASCII filename parameters.

CVE-2011-2732 describes Spring Security header injection and HTTP response splitting in affected 2.0.0 through 2.0.6 and 3.0.0 through 3.0.5 releases. The failed new-unified row uses exact source snapshot checkout beb0ec4ba95265a7e3481b3eb8d87f3b922733ae, which is the peeled commit for tag 2.0.6.RELEASE and is in the affected 2.0.x range. The public advisory states that Spring Security allowed a request parameter named spring-security-redirect by default to determine the redirect target after login, and that the shared base functionality also affected logout handling so CRLF characters in a maliciously constructed logout URL could inject headers or split the response. In the exact checkout, TargetUrlResolverImpl defines DEFAULT_TARGET_PARAMETER as spring-security-redirect, reads currentRequest.getParameter(targetUrlParameter), URL-decodes it, and returns it as the target URL. AbstractProcessingFilter uses this resolver during successful authentication, then passes the resulting targetUrl to sendRedirect(), which delegates to RedirectUtils.sendRedirect(). RedirectUtils constructs finalUrl and calls response.sendRedirect(response.encodeRedirectURL(finalUrl)) without rejecting CR or LF. The logout path in LogoutFilter similarly derives a request-controlled target URL from the logoutSuccessUrl request parameter or other request-derived fallback and delegates to the same RedirectUtils.sendRedirect() helper. In the same checkout, DefaultHttpFirewall.getFirewalledResponse() returns the raw response, so there is no response wrapper guard against CR/LF in redirect locations. Fix commit f5fbda42e5f494f1a8aa96a0f8b35d60a4f57556, titled SEC-1790: Reject redirect locations containing CR or LF, changes DefaultHttpFirewall to wrap responses in FirewalledResponse and adds FirewalledResponse.sendRedirect(String) that throws IllegalArgumentException when the redirect location contains carriage return or line feed before delegating to the underlying response. This binds the advisory to source-backed request-controlled redirect target flow and the production fix that rejects CR/LF at the redirect response boundary.

CVE-2025-22223 / GHSA-hh3m-g4qj-4835 describes a Spring Security authorization bypass for method security annotations on parameterized types. The advisory states that Spring Security 6.4.0 through 6.4.3 can miss method security annotations placed on a parameterized superclass, interface, or overridden method when the concrete target method itself has no annotation, allowing the target method to be invoked without proper authorization. The failed new-unified row uses exact source snapshot checkout 4993fa863a02008b606044cb897db6b54ec116f0, an affected 6.4.x source snapshot before fixed release 6.4.4. GitHub compare from this checkout to tag 6.4.4 shows fix commit dc2e1af2dab8ef81cd4edd25b56a2babeaab8cf9 as the first commit ahead. In the exact checkout, AuthorizationManagerBeforeMethodInterceptor.preAuthorize() installs PreAuthorizeAuthorizationManager for @PreAuthorize method security. During invocation, attemptAuthorization() calls authorizationManager.authorize(); if the result is null, the interceptor does not deny and proceeds with the method invocation. PreAuthorizeAuthorizationManager.check() obtains an ExpressionAttribute from PreAuthorizeExpressionAttributeRegistry and returns null when the registry reports ExpressionAttribute.NULL_ATTRIBUTE. The registry calls SecurityAnnotationScanners.requireUnique(PreAuthorize.class) and scans the invoked method plus target class. UniqueSecurityAnnotationScanner.findMethodAnnotations() delegates to findClosestMethodAnnotations(), but the vulnerable implementation locates overridden methods with targetClass.getDeclaredMethod(method.getName(), method.getParameterTypes()). For parameterized interfaces, superclasses, or generic overridden methods, the concrete method parameter types can differ from the generic declaration after type resolution, so getDeclaredMethod() can throw NoSuchMethodException and the scanner moves on without finding the inherited @PreAuthorize annotation. With no discovered annotation, requireUnique() returns null, the registry emits NULL_ATTRIBUTE, PreAuthorizeAuthorizationManager returns null, and the before-method interceptor treats the invocation as authorized. Fix commit dc2e1af2, titled Align Method Traversal with MergedAnnotations, replaces direct getDeclaredMethod() lookup with findMethod()/isOverride()/hasSameGenericTypeParameters() using ResolvableType and adds regression tests for annotations on parameterized interface, parameterized superclass, and parameterized method. This binds the advisory to source-backed method-security annotation traversal and the production fix that resolves generic override relationships.

CVE-2025-22228 describes Spring Security BCryptPasswordEncoder failing to enforce BCrypt's maximum effective password length. The Spring advisory states that BCryptPasswordEncoder.matches(CharSequence,String) incorrectly returns true for passwords larger than 72 characters as long as the first 72 characters are the same, affecting Spring Security 6.3.0 through 6.3.7 among other lines and fixed in 6.3.8. The failed new-unified row uses exact source snapshot checkout 36ea1b11a7dae7904e3c70b5e10fb01152fec5d4, which belongs to the affected 6.3.7 line. GitHub compare from this checkout to tag 6.3.8 shows fix commit 46f0dc6dfc8402cd556c598fdf2d31f9d46cdbf3, titled Enforce BCrypt password length, before the 6.3.8 release commit. In the exact checkout, BCryptPasswordEncoder.matches() accepts rawPassword, validates only null/empty/hash-format conditions, and delegates rawPassword.toString() plus the stored hash to BCrypt.checkpw(). BCrypt.checkpw(String,String) converts the full plaintext to UTF-8 bytes and calls hashpwforcheck(passwordb, hashed), which delegates to hashpw(passwordb, salt, true). The vulnerable hashpw(byte[], String, boolean) validates salt and rounds but has no check that passwordb.length is at most 72 bytes before it appends the minor-version NUL byte and invokes crypt_raw(). crypt_raw() feeds the password bytes into ekskey() and repeated key() expansion; BCrypt's algorithm has a 72-byte effective password limit, so two longer candidate passwords with identical first 72 bytes can hash equivalently against the same stored bcrypt hash. Fix commit 46f0dc6d adds an explicit passwordb.length > 72 IllegalArgumentException at the beginning of hashpw(byte[], String, boolean) and adds a regression test where 72 characters match but 73 characters throw. This binds the advisory to source-backed BCryptPasswordEncoder.matches password verification and the production fix that enforces the 72-byte limit before bcrypt hashing/checking.

CVE-2018-1000850 describes a Retrofit 2.x before 2.5.0 directory/path traversal issue in RequestBuilder.addPathParameter/addPathParam where attacker-controlled encoded @Path values can manipulate the resolved relative URL for POST, PUT, or DELETE requests. In the reviewed exact source snapshot 7158698314daa138e993fac6a590ed19d78a8599, ServiceMethod parses interface @Path annotations into ParameterHandler.Path while preserving path.encoded(), and ServiceMethod.toCall() applies each handler to a RequestBuilder. ParameterHandler.Path converts the runtime argument and calls RequestBuilder.addPathParam(name, convertedValue, encoded). In 2.4.0 addPathParam directly replaces the URL template placeholder with canonicalizeForPath(value, encoded). canonicalizeForPath deliberately leaves slash and percent characters unencoded when encoded=true, so an attacker-supplied encoded path segment containing dot or dot-dot semantics can become part of the relative URL and is later resolved by baseUrl.resolve(relativeUrl) or baseUrl.newBuilder(relativeUrl). The 2.5.0 changelog explicitly records Prevent @Path values from participating in path-traversal, and the fixed 2.5.0 RequestBuilder adds PATH_TRAVERSAL detection plus a throw in the same addPathParam block after computing newRelativeUrl, including percent-encoded dot segments.

CVE-2018-1002202 / SNYK-JAVA-NETLINGALAZIP4J-31679 describes a Zip Slip arbitrary file write in net.lingala.zip4j:zip4j before 1.3.3, where a crafted zip entry path can escape the intended extraction directory during archive extraction. The failed new-unified row uses exact source snapshot checkout d87ffa2d64ffb3a0a1cf0c7a69c7b19d7015bfde. The M17 registry binds this case to zip4j 1.3.2 and the declared source repository iris-sast/zip4j, where tag 1.3.2 points to this checkout with commit message Add decompiled source for 1.3.2 (vulnerable) from zip4j-1.3.2-sources.jar. The upstream srikanth-lingala/zip4j repository does not expose this old 1.3.2 source snapshot, but the failed case already treats this exact source snapshot as its checkout; the reviewed evidence therefore uses source-backed spans from that exact checkout while preserving the normalized repo_key. In the exact checkout, ZipFile.extractAll validates only the destination folder and then passes all FileHeader entries to Unzip.extractAll(). ZipFile.extractFile delegates a selected FileHeader to FileHeader.extractFile(), which validates the output folder and calls Unzip.extractFile(). Unzip.initExtractFile() obtains fileHeader.getFileName(), ensures outPath has a trailing separator, and for directories constructs completePath = outPath + fileName and creates directories. For files, checkOutputDirectoryStructure() similarly sets fileName from fileHeader.getFileName() unless a caller-supplied newFileName overrides it, constructs compOutPath = outPath + fileName, and creates the parent directory. UnzipEngine.unzipFile() then opens getOutputStream(outPath, newFileName), copies zip entry bytes to that output stream, and applies attributes to new File(getOutputFileNameWithPath(outPath, newFileName)). The vulnerable 1.3.2 code does not canonicalize the combined output path or check that it remains under the canonical output directory, so a file header name containing ../ can cause writes outside the destination directory. The fixed 1.3.3 source snapshot 59aeea594ff885e06c25751dc6334dfea1bed8c6 adds a canonical containment check at the start of Unzip.initExtractFile(): it builds fileName and completePath, compares new File(completePath).getCanonicalPath() with new File(outPath).getCanonicalPath(), and throws ZipException when the entry escapes the target directory. This binds the advisory to source-backed archive extraction path construction and the fixed 1.3.3 containment check.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2014-7816 describes Undertow 1.0.x before 1.0.17.Final, 1.1.x before 1.1.0.CR5, and 1.2.x before 1.2.0.Beta3 on Windows allowing arbitrary file reads through directory traversal in a resource URI. In the reviewed exact source snapshot 4aa98c80fa9962235c94f8666c30793d0018f95d, ResourceHandler.serveResource() directly passes exchange.getRelativePath() to resourceManager.getResource() and then serves the returned Resource; DefaultServlet.doGet() likewise takes getPath(req), only applies extension allow/deny checks, and calls resourceManager.getResource(path). CanonicalPathUtils.canonicalize() recognizes forward slash as the only path separator for dot-segment folding, so Windows backslash separators do not participate in canonicalization before resource lookup. ServletPathMatches.findWelcomeFile() also concatenates path plus welcome-file name and calls resourceManager.getResource() without rejecting Windows separators. The 1.0.17.Final fix commit ab8ba2adc9ca508dc22e41f1b63c34c5a78e80a1 is titled UNDERTOW-338 Fix tirectory traversal attack on windows; its diff adds PathSeparatorHandler to replace File.separatorChar with slash and canonicalize request, relative, and resolved paths on non-slash platforms, changes ResourceHandler to canonicalize relative paths and skip resource lookup when a non-slash separator remains, changes DefaultServlet to replace/canonicalize Windows separators and reject paths still containing File.separator, and changes ServletPathMatches.findWelcomeFile() to return null when a non-slash separator is present.

CVE-2025-48881 / GHSA-965r-9cg9-g42p describes missing authorization in valtimo-backend-libraries before 12.13.0.RELEASE: users who can reach object-management configured objects, or direct object URLs exposed elsewhere, can list, view, create, modify, or delete Objecten API objects without the intended object-level permissions. The reviewed vulnerable checkout is 33779f203273a6b02007217965d97d5036178d8e. The fix commit 6ab04b30d3dab816bfea32d40ba50e5dd4517272 has this exact checkout as its sole parent and is titled Added permission check for objecten api objects. In the vulnerable parent, ObjectManagementHttpSecurityConfigurer marks /api/v1/object/management/configuration/{id}/object GET and POST only as authenticated. ObjectManagementResource exposes those list/search endpoints. ObjectManagementFacade then delegates object read/list/create/update/delete operations to ObjectenApiPlugin, and ObjectenApiPlugin delegates all of those operations to ObjectenApiClient. In ObjectenApiClient at the vulnerable checkout, the constructor accepts only RestClient.Builder, OutboxService, and ObjectMapper, and each get/list/create/patch/update/delete method directly calls the remote Objecten API and emits outbox events without AuthorizationService.requirePermission or ObjectActionProvider checks. The fix adds an AuthorizationService dependency, objectenapi authorization enablement, ObjectActionProvider actions VIEW/VIEW_LIST/CREATE/MODIFY/DELETE, ObjectSpecificationFactory, PBAC permission configuration, and requirePermission calls in ObjectenApiClient for the affected methods. These source-backed spans therefore bind the missing authorization root cause to the exact vulnerable checkout and the corrective patch.

CVE-2018-12542 describes a Vert.x Web StaticHandler path traversal issue on Windows: StaticHandler uses external request path input to construct a pathname intended to remain inside the configured web root, but vulnerable versions 3.0.0 through 3.5.3 do not neutralize backslash path-separator sequences that Windows treats as filesystem separators. In the reviewed exact source snapshot 3fe3873cc28b4d833c90f8989ff797a7b463da2c, StaticHandlerImpl.handle() decodes context.normalisedPath() and immediately calls Utils.removeDots(), whose implementation only treats forward slash as the path separator. The resulting path is passed to sendStatic(), getFile() concatenates webRoot with Utils.pathOffset(path, context), and the handler then checks existence/properties and eventually serves the computed file path through HttpServerResponse.sendFile(). The fixed 3.5.4 StaticHandlerImpl changes this same handle() path: after urlDecode(), when File.separatorChar is not forward slash, it replaces the platform separator with forward slash before calling Utils.removeDots(). That fix binds the public Windows separator traversal advisory to the vulnerable exact checkout, the StaticHandler request path source, insufficient separator normalization, webRoot path construction, and file serving sink.

CVE-2019-17640 describes a Vert.x Web StaticHandler Windows path traversal issue where backslash separators in the request path were not normalized before static file resolution, allowing a path to escape the configured web root. In the reviewed exact source snapshot 2146b7240096e25b40bb1acc083fa7ec79330989, StaticHandlerImpl.handle() accepts GET and HEAD requests, URL-decodes context.normalisedPath(), and directly calls HttpUtils.removeDots() without first replacing backslashes with forward slashes. The resulting path flows through sendStatic(), getFile(), and Utils.pathOffset() into a filesystem path formed as webRoot plus the route-adjusted request path, then non-directory files are served through HttpServerResponse.sendFile(). The fixed 3.9.4 and 4.0.0.CR1 StaticHandlerImpl sources change the same handle() block to decode into uriDecodedPath and call HttpUtils.removeDots(uriDecodedPath.replace(\, /)), making Windows backslashes participate in dot-segment normalization before file resolution.

CVE-2022-23082 / GHSA-m9vj-44f3-78xw describes a path traversal flaw in io.whitesource:curekit before 1.1.4: FileSecurityUtils.isFileOutsideDir fails to sanitize/validate user-controlled paths correctly, allowing sibling paths such as /usr/foo-bar to be treated as inside /usr/foo. The failed new-unified row uses exact checkout 7b275a67a5992165deb186b2b3f7764ddd062d26, which is tag v1.1.3 and whose pom.xml declares io.whitesource:curekit version 1.1.3. In that checkout, FileSecurityUtils.isFileOutsideDir constructs File objects for filePath and baseDirPath, canonicalizes both as strings, and returns !file.getCanonicalPath().startsWith(baseDir.getCanonicalPath()). This canonical string prefix check lacks path-boundary semantics: an attacker-controlled file path that canonicalizes to a sibling path sharing the same prefix as the base directory can make startsWith(baseCanonical) return true, causing isFileOutsideDir to return false and incorrectly classify the outside path as inside the base directory. The v1.1.4 fix commit af35e870ed09411d2f1fae6db1b04598cd1a31b6 is the tag v1.1.4 commit and contains two patch hunks for this method: first adding a trailing separator to the base canonical path, then replacing String.startsWith with file.getCanonicalFile().toPath().startsWith(baseDir.getCanonicalFile().toPath()). The same fix adds a regression test with taintedInput /usr/foo/../foo-bar/bar and baseDir /usr/foo expecting isFileOutsideDir to return true. These spans bind the advisory to the exact vulnerable v1.1.3 source and the source-backed fix that restores path-component-aware containment validation.

CVE-2018-1047 / GHSA-fmr4-w67p-vh8x describes a path traversal information disclosure in org.wildfly:wildfly-undertow before 12.0.0, specifically through org.wildfly.extension.undertow.deployment.ServletResourceManager.getResource. The failed new-unified row uses exact checkout 4fd7bffaf2ee73201910684f2674aa1bced7fe81, the 11.0.0.Final source snapshot. In that checkout, ServletResourceManager.getResource first delegates to the deployment PathResourceManager. If that does not find a resource, it strips one leading slash from the request path and enters the servlet overlay branch. CVE-2025-23367 / GHSA-QR6X-62GQ-4CCP describes a WildFly Core RBAC access-control flaw where a user without write privileges, such as Monitor or Auditor, could suspend or resume the server because the suspend and resume operation handlers did not perform authorization checks. The original IRIS registry identity for this case refers to wildfly-core_CVE-2025-23367_27.0.0.Beta7, and the exact vulnerable checkout fef25f1036b0eee858261d892bfdca5fd86b0a50 is the WildFly Core 27.0.0.Beta7 tag. The same missing-check pattern remains in 27.0.0.Final, and the public advisory lists 27.0.1.Final as patched. In the vulnerable checkout, ServerRootResourceDefinition registers SUSPEND and RESUME operation handlers for running-server lifecycle operations. ServerSuspendHandler.execute acquires the controller lock, normalizes timeout, schedules a RUNTIME step, and directly calls suspendController.suspend(ServerSuspendController.Context.RUNNING) without calling context.authorize(...WRITE_RUNTIME). ServerResumeHandler.execute similarly schedules a RUNTIME step and directly calls suspendController.resume(...). The fixed 27.0.1.Final tag cd47c62e654de3b02f170c541870f2f09270309e imports Action and AuthorizationResult, calls context.authorize(operation, EnumSet.of(Action.ActionEffect.WRITE_RUNTIME)) inside both RUNTIME steps, and throws ControllerLogger.ACCESS_LOGGER.unauthorized(...) on DENY before changing server state. This binds the public RBAC advisory to exact source-backed suspend/resume handlers and the fixed authorization boundary.

CVE-2013-7285 / GHSA-F554-X222-WGF7 describes command execution during XStream unmarshalling before 1.4.7 when the security framework has not been initialized. The failed new-unified row uses exact checkout 768c6e417a75e7732fc591bee844e5e81af56a7d, which is tag XSTREAM_1_4_6 and whose pom.xml declares XStream 1.4.6. In this checkout, XStream.fromXML overloads directly create a HierarchicalStreamReader and call unmarshal() with the default mapper/converter chain. buildMapper() creates DefaultMapper, DynamicProxyMapper, aliasing mappers, and other mappers, but there is no SecurityMapper in the chain and no addPermission/allowTypes API. DefaultMapper.realClass resolves XML element or class attribute names into Java classes using the configured ClassLoader. DynamicProxyConverter.unmarshal reads interface names and a handler class attribute from XML, resolves both with mapper.realClass, builds a proxy, and calls context.convertAnother(proxy, handlerType). ReflectionConverter.canConvert(type) returns canAccess(type) for any accessible type, including java.beans.EventHandler in 1.4.6. AbstractReflectionConverter then instantiates and populates arbitrary objects during unmarshal. The 1.4.7 compare and release notes state that the release addresses CVE-2013-7285 arbitrary execution of commands when unmarshalling, adds a security framework to fine-control unmarshalled types, and makes java.beans.EventHandler no longer handled automatically. The security fix adds SecurityVulnerabilityTest with an XML dynamic-proxy handler class java.beans.EventHandler invoking a Run target and expecting XStreamException unless EventHandler is explicitly registered; it also changes ReflectionConverter.canConvert to reject EventHandler by default and adds the new SecurityMapper/TypePermission framework. These source-backed spans bind the vulnerable 1.4.6 unmarshalling path to arbitrary class/EventHandler instantiation and the 1.4.7 fix that blocks this dangerous type by default and adds type permissions.

CVE-2020-26217 describes XStream before 1.4.14 allowing local attackers to execute arbitrary shell commands during unmarshalling by using a Java runtime gadget chain such as java.lang.ProcessBuilder. The reviewed prepatch checkout cba30d7f75cb0f7e2fd66c03989e51f7c8521232 is the peeled XSTREAM_1_4_13 release tag. In that checkout, XStream.setupSecurity installs AnyTypePermission.ANY and only explicitly denies java.beans.EventHandler plus two regexp families for lazy iterators and javax.crypto types. It does not deny java.lang.ProcessBuilder or javax.imageio.ImageIO$ContainsFilter by default. The same prepatch tree exposes denyTypes and denyTypesByRegExp APIs and contains SecurityVulnerabilityTest coverage for EventHandler and Void, showing the intended security boundary and the previously covered dangerous-runtime types. The official XStream CVE page for CVE-2020-26217 states that version 1.4.14 fixes the issue and gives a workaround denying javax.imageio.ImageIO$ContainsFilter and java.lang.ProcessBuilder, plus EventHandler and Void for older versions. The 1.4.14 source jar shows the exact fix in XStream.setupSecurity: the default denyTypes list changes from only java.beans.EventHandler to java.beans.EventHandler, java.lang.ProcessBuilder, and javax.imageio.ImageIO$ContainsFilter. These spans bind the vulnerable 1.4.13 source behavior to the 1.4.14 default security hardening.

CVE-2023-32697 is a sqlite-jdbc remote code execution vulnerability when the JDBC URL is attacker controlled. The GitHub advisory lists affected versions through 3.41.2.1 and points to release 3.41.2.2; that release includes fix commit edb4b8adc2447bc04e05b9b908195a4bc7926242, fix: use random UUID for external resources. In the reviewed 3.41.2.1 source snapshot, JDBC.createConnection() passes the attacker-controlled URL-derived address into SQLiteConnection, SQLiteConnection.open() accepts :resource: database names, resolves missing classpath resources as arbitrary URLs, and calls extractResource(). extractResource() writes non-file resources to java.io.tmpdir using a deterministic file name based on resourceAddr.hashCode(), reuses a pre-existing newer temp file, or deletes and replaces it before NativeDB opens the resulting file. The fix changes that deterministic temp file name to UUID.randomUUID(), confirming the source-backed vulnerable path.

The MITRE CVE record for CVE-2020-29204 describes XXL-JOB 2.2.0 stored XSS in Add User, specifically a bypass of the 20-character limit via xxl-job-admin/src/main/java/com/xxl/job/admin/controller/UserController.java. The exact failed new-unified checkout 1874c4854f81d6af4a9471d3fe111cdbf713f336 is the v2.2.0 tag and pom.xml declares version 2.2.0. Upstream issue #2083 is titled v2.2.0 Add User Stored XSS vulnerabilities, Escape 20 length limit and gives a 20-character payload shape <script/src=//14.rs> that automatically triggers after being added. In the reviewed 2.2.0 source, UserController.add accepts XxlJobUser from /user/add, trims username, validates only presence and a length range of 4 to 20, and then calls xxlJobUserDao.save without server-side character allowlisting, HTML escaping, or sanitization. The MyBatis XxlJobUserMapper.save statement persists #{username} directly into xxl_job_user.username, and pageList later returns XxlJobUser rows directly in the JSON data list. The user management page defines a username column bound to the server-provided username field, while the add form stricter alphanumeric validation exists only in client-side JavaScript and can be bypassed by posting directly to /user/add. These source-backed spans bind the stored payload entry point, persistence sink, and management-page recall surface for the stored XSS described by CVE-2020-29204.

CVE-2022-24897 / GHSA-cvx5-m8vg-vxgc describes XWiki Commons Velocity scripts not being properly sandboxed against Java File API read or write operations, patched in 12.6.7, 12.10.3, and 13.0RC1. The exact failed new-unified checkout 4f33e1efd74016fa9eb31b3c2fcd01bc6becd551 is the peeled xwiki-commons-12.6.6 tag and pom.xml declares xwiki-commons version 12.6.6, immediately before the 12.6.7 patch line. In this checkout, DefaultVelocityConfiguration installs SecureUberspector as the first default Velocity uberspector, and DefaultVelocityEngine initializes RuntimeInstance with those properties before evaluating templates. SecureUberspector constructs SecureIntrospector from configured bad classes and packages. SecureIntrospector only adds special allowlist handling for selected Class methods and otherwise delegates to SecureIntrospectorImpl.checkObjectExecutePermission; it has no File-specific allowlist or deny handling, leaving File write methods such as mkdir and renameTo outside the XWiki-specific sandbox policy. The 12.6.7 compare changes SecureIntrospector to import java.io.File, maintain per-class whitelistedMethods, add prepareWhiteListFile for selected safe File methods, and change checkObjectExecutePermission so File and subclasses are allowed only if the requested method is in that whitelist. The new SecureIntrospectorTest asserts File.toString is allowed while File.mkdir, File.renameTo, and CustomFile.mkdir are denied. These source-backed spans bind the vulnerable 12.6.6 Velocity sandbox behavior to the File API write access fixed in 12.6.7.

CVE-2023-29201 affects org.xwiki.commons:xwiki-commons-xml before 14.6-rc-1. The advisory states that restricted-mode HTML cleaning did not include an allowlist filter for HTML elements and attributes, allowing XSS and possible server-side code execution when privileged users viewed malicious content. The frozen registry's declared 14.6-rc-1 checkout 5d9632d9471f315052c76d7699a17414524ea093 is the patched release tag, so this reviewed-source row binds the case to the prepatch 14.5 release checkout bae1e23e73cafc007e5f28b39a04bfa0acf0199c. In the 14.5 xwiki-commons-xml source, HTMLCleanerConfiguration defines the restricted cleaning parameter, DefaultHTMLCleaner applies only control, body, list item, list, font, attribute, and link filters, and the component list contains no sanitizer component. In 14.6-rc-1, the XML module adds HTMLElementSanitizer, SecureHTMLElementSanitizer, HTML/SVG/MathML definitions, and SanitizerFilter. SanitizerFilter runs only when HTMLCleanerConfiguration.RESTRICTED is true, removing disallowed elements and attributes using HTMLElementSanitizer; SecureHTMLElementSanitizer implements element and attribute allowlists and rejects dangerous URI values such as script/data protocols unless explicitly allowed. These source spans bind the vulnerable prepatch absence of restricted-mode sanitizer enforcement to the 14.6-rc-1 fix.

CVE-2023-31126 / GHSA-pv7v-ph6g-3gxv describes XWiki Commons XML HTML sanitizer accepting invalid characters in data attribute names, enabling arbitrary HTML injection; the advisory states this does not affect restricted HTMLCleaner mode because attributes are cleaned there, and it was patched in XWiki 14.10.4 and 15.0RC1 by ensuring data attributes contain only allowed characters. The exact failed new-unified checkout 011dee864805aec0b24151f69f230a42e40087da is the xwiki-commons-14.10.3 source snapshot and pom.xml declares version 14.10.3, immediately before the fixed 14.10.4 release. In this checkout, DefaultHTMLCleaner parses HTML and applies configured filters after serialization, including the sanitizer filter. SecureHTMLElementSanitizer defines DATA_ATTR as a prefix regex ^data-[\-\w.\u00B7-\uFFFF] and then calls matcher(lowerAttribute).find() in isAttributeAllowed. This accepts any attribute whose name merely contains a matching data-* prefix, including names with invalid trailing characters such as data-x/test or data-x>test, and returns true before falling through to normal allowlist/value validation. The 14.10.4 tag dfd0eff6a9f28f5a8840a5e4a51f0a24524c0280 replaces DATA_ATTR with a full XML-compatible data attribute pattern ending in +$, switches the check to .matches(), and adds dataAttributes tests that reject data-, data-x/test, data-x>test, and data-x:y while accepting valid data-a and data-x-wiki.test_ƒ. These source-backed spans bind the vulnerable 14.10.3 data-attribute sanitizer decision to the 14.10.4 fix.

CVE-2023-32070 affects XWiki Rendering before 14.6-rc-1: XHTML/HTML rendering did not check dangerous attributes and attribute values, allowing XSS through attributes and link URLs supported by XWiki syntax. The frozen registry's declared 14.6-rc-1 checkout 48b2970c152accd0d9dbc461a2f04bb36686491e is the patched release tag, so this reviewed-source row binds the case to the prepatch 14.5 release checkout 9eae915967e41a40715caac41b1ad3464ef343b5. In the 14.5 xwiki-rendering-xml source, XHTMLWikiPrinter overrides printXMLElement and printXMLStartElement overloads only to handle whitespace, then directly delegates to XMLWikiPrinter with the caller-provided attributes. XMLWikiPrinter then adds those attributes to a DOM4J Element or forwards SAX Attributes directly to xmlWriter.startElement without any HTML element/attribute sanitizer. In 14.6-rc-1, XHTMLWikiPrinter imports HTMLElementSanitizer, stores an optional sanitizer, checks isElementAllowed before printing elements, and routes all attribute-bearing printXMLElement/printXMLStartElement overloads through cleanAttributes. The cleanAttributes methods call htmlElementSanitizer.isAttributeAllowed and translate disallowed attribute names with the data-xwiki-translated-attribute- prefix rather than rendering them as active attributes. These source spans bind the prepatch attribute passthrough behavior to the 14.6-rc-1 rendering sanitizer fix.

In this checkout, XHTMLWikiPrinter defines TRANSLATED_ATTRIBUTE_PREFIX as data-xwiki-translated-attribute-. The three cleanAttributes overloads for Map, String[][], and SAX Attributes each call htmlElementSanitizer.isAttributeAllowed on the original attribute; when the sanitizer rejects it, the code directly adds or returns TRANSLATED_ATTRIBUTE_PREFIX plus the original attribute name, with no removal of invalid data-attribute characters and no second sanitizer check on the generated translated attribute name. provenance.rationale: CVE-2023-45277 describes Yamcs 5.8.6 storage API directory traversal in which the API can escape a filesystem bucket base directory and read arbitrary files. The exact failed new-unified checkout 9443a67d2aeda20fb73f68c5d571b515d68c05e4 is tag yamcs-5.8.6 and the root, yamcs-api, and yamcs-core POMs declare version 5.8.6. In this checkout, buckets.proto exposes GET /api/buckets/{instance}/{bucketName}/objects/{objectName*} and /api/storage/buckets/{bucketName}/objects/{objectName*}; the wildcard objectName is stored in GetObjectRequest.objectName. BucketsApi.getObject reads request.getObjectName(), resolves the bucket, then calls bucket.findObject(objName) and bucket.getObject(objName) without calling verifyObjectName or applying any path containment check at the HTTP layer. For filesystem buckets, FileSystemBucket stores a root Path, but findObject directly executes root.resolve(objectName), checks Files.exists, and reads attributes, while getObject directly executes root.resolve(objectName) and returns Files.readAllBytes(path). The only canonical containment check in the vulnerable snapshot appears in putObject, so read-side find/get can resolve traversal components outside root. The upstream source-backed fix commit b6db35e432e62fdff0447cf513369f0b8a848abf, titled 'Fix traversal vuln. on fs buckets. Reported by @visionspacetec', changes getObject, findObject, deleteObject, and putObject to call a common resolvePath helper, and resolvePath rejects paths whose canonical path does not start with the bucket root canonical path. These spans bind the CVE-2023-45277 arbitrary file-read behavior to the exact yamcs-5.8.6 source snapshot and the later filesystem-bucket traversal fix.
